## Phase K79 · Grouped Customer-Facing Estimate Line Items — SHIPPED (Feb 2026)

**Scope**: Estimates only (invoices out of scope). Rolls line items up by K71 `service_category_id` for customer-facing surfaces (email link, portal, PDF). Admin view stays fully itemized.

**Delivery**
- **Schema**: `customer_group_display: bool` (default `true` for new quotes, `false` after backfill) + `customer_group_descriptions: Dict[service_category_id, str]` on `db.quotes`. Both live on the doc (not per-line).
- **Aggregation helper**: `backend/services/quotes/customer_view.py` — pure functions `group_lines_for_customer()` + `build_customer_view_payload()`. Groups by `service_category_id` in first-appearance order; ungrouped lines bucket into "Other" at the tail; `long_description` NEVER read (contract-tested).
- **Endpoints**: `GET /api/quotes/{qid}/customer-view` (bearer auth) + `GET /api/portal/quotes/via-token/customer-view` (magic-link). `GET /estimates/{eid}/full` now embeds a `customer_view` block. `GET /estimates/{eid}/pdf` forks 3 modes: admin internal PDF (`?internal=1`, 6-col itemized), customer grouped, customer itemized fallback. `POST /quotes` seeds `customer_group_display=true`. `PUT /quotes/{id}` accepts both new fields.
- **Admin editor** (`<K79CustomerViewSection>`): checkbox + per-service-category description editor (250-char cap, one row per unique category in `line_items`) + "Preview customer view" button (`<K79CustomerViewPreview>` modal renders grouped rendering with WIP state — admin sees pending description text before saving).
- **Customer surfaces**: `<EstimateView>` renders grouped rows when `as_customer && customer_view.customer_group_display`. Portal quote view + email link pick it up automatically.
- **Migration**: `scripts/k79_customer_group_display_migration.py` — idempotent, writes audit doc to `migration_runs`. **Run on preview**: 124 existing quotes backfilled to `false`; follow-up run reported `status: noop`.

**Long-description contract locked at 4 layers**: helper never reads it · helper test asserts scrub · endpoint test asserts scrub · Vitest asserts scrub in both grouped + itemized preview modes.

## Phase K80.a · Add + Delete Line-Item Affordances on `K71LineItemsEditor` — SHIPPED (Feb 2026)

**Scope**: Frontend only. Close the K80-recon feature gap: staff could not add lines to a saved estimate/quote, and could not delete lines from a saved doc through the K71 surface. K80.b (server-side status gating on `PUT /quotes/{id}`) is deliberately queued as a separate phase.

**Delivery**
- `K71LineItemsEditor` gains `+ Add line` button under the table (visible only when `canEdit`). Clicking appends an empty scaffolded row and enters inline-edit mode on it. Cancel on a NEW line discards it entirely (no phantom empty rows).
- Trash icon per row (visible only when `canEdit`). Clicking removes the row locally and mounts a dark undo toast (`k71-undo-toast`) with an Undo button for 5 seconds. Undo restores the row at its original index; timeout commits `onLinesUpdated` with the deleted row excluded.
- Only one pending delete at a time — Add-line and other trash buttons disable during the undo window (dimmed with tooltip).
- Category-required validation reused unchanged: an added line without Service + Income category can't be saved; added-then-cancelled rows never round-trip.
- Discoverability fix on `QuoteInvoiceDetail.jsx`: the `Edit invoice` button (which opens `InvoiceEditModal`) is now **hidden on draft invoices** (K71 covers add/edit/delete), kept visible on `sent`/`paid`/`void`/`cancelled` where the modal's typed-confirm UX matters. Relabelled to `Edit invoice (advanced)` with a tooltip.

**Tests**
- `test/k71-line-items-editor.test.jsx` — +11 K80.a cases (18 total pass). Covers: visibility gates on canEdit, add appends empty row in edit mode, Cancel on new line removes it, add+save without categories → inline errors + no commit, trash hides row + shows undo toast + no commit yet, Undo restores row + cancels pending commit, timeout commits with deleted row excluded.
- Full suite: **477 files pass · 1 skipped (Hygiene B) · 3758 tests pass · 34 skipped (Hygiene B untouched)**.

**Files touched**
- `frontend/src/components/quotes/K71LineItemsEditor.jsx` — rewrite with local state (localItems, editIndex, newLineIndex, pendingDelete + ref for delayed commit), Add/Delete/Undo UX, unmount cleanup.
- `frontend/src/pages/quotes/QuoteInvoiceDetail.jsx` — gate `Edit invoice` button behind non-draft status; relabel.
- `frontend/src/test/k71-line-items-editor.test.jsx` — +11 assertions.

**Guardrails held**
- Zero backend changes.
- 34 Hygiene B skips untouched.
- No I1.5 / I1.7.a / I1.7.b code touched.
- K71 category-required rule intact.
- No new colors outside token vocabulary (delete uses `#DC2626` matching K71 error convention; undo toast uses `#1F2937` slate + `#F9FAFB` on-surface — bounded to the toast).

## Phase K63.finalize · All ingress paths wired + resend endpoint — SHIPPED (Feb 2026, preview only)

**Scope:** Backend + Web. K63 is now feature-complete —
every runtime lead-insertion path either fires the dispatcher
or has a documented intentional exclusion.

**Delivery**
- Wired `send_lead_alert_notifications` into the four remaining
  ingress paths:
  * `routers/portal_referrals.py` — customer-portal referral
    submission (added `BackgroundTasks` to handler).
  * `routers/property.py` — property-lookup / virtual-bid lead
    capture (added `BackgroundTasks` to handler).
  * `routers/d2d.py` — door-to-door `interested`/`sold` capture
    across all three call sites (`POST /api/d2d/knocks`,
    `PUT /api/d2d/knocks/{id}`, `POST /api/d2d/knocks/{id}/convert`)
    via a new optional `background_tasks` arg on `_sync_lead`.
  * `routers/ringcentral.py` — inbound RC missed-call webhook.
    Webhook has no FastAPI-injected `BackgroundTasks`, so a local
    instance is created and drained inline (RC tolerates
    multi-second latency and the path only fires on unknown
    callers, so cost is naturally low).
- `server.py:1777` verdict — intentionally NOT wired. It's the
  RC nightly contact-book sync (`source: "rc-contact-sync"`),
  a bulk contact-import cron that could import hundreds of rows
  per run. Documented in-code + in the K63 ingress inventory.
- New endpoint `POST /api/admin/leads/{id}/resend-notifications`
  in `routers/admin_resend_lead_notifications.py`:
  * `require_admin` (admin, super_admin, owner).
  * Tenant-scoped (404 on cross-tenant).
  * Clears the `lead_notification_dispatches` rows for the
    (tenant, lead) pair to bypass idempotency, then invokes the
    dispatcher.
  * Writes `audit_logs.event = "lead_notification_resent"` with
    the actor identity.
- Frontend: "Resend alerts" button on `LeadDetail` (admin-only).
  Confirmation modal warns about the idempotency bypass; result
  panel renders every dispatched (channel, recipient) pair with
  full test-id coverage.

**Tests**

## Phase K30.copy-admin-link · Super-admin clipboard copy of reset URL — SHIPPED (Feb 2026)

**Scope:** Backend + Web (mobile untouched). Standing order
honored (bbeck169/Pool-Landscaping.git ignored).

**Purpose** — Give super-admins a way to mint a fresh
password-reset URL for a customer and copy it directly to their
clipboard for phone-support scenarios where email deliverability
would be too slow. Never emailed on this path.

**Backend**
- New endpoint `POST /api/customers/{cid}/portal-reset-link-copy`
  in `portal_admin.py` gated by `require_super_admin` (stricter
  than the send path's admin gate because the response body
  carries a bearer credential).
- Returns `{ok, reset_url, expires_at, token_ttl_minutes,
  provisioned_user}`. Token source tag
  `admin_reset_link_copy` distinguishes copy-path tokens from
  send-path tokens in `password_reset_tokens`.
- Audit event `admin_password_reset_copied` written on every
  call; token value NEVER logged (grep-asserted in tests).
- `portal_history` widens the surfaced-event list to include the
  new event so the activity feed shows both send + copy actions.

  button beside "Send reset link", gated by
  `canCopyResetLink(role)` (new exported helper returning true
  only for `super_admin`). Button is invisible for non-super
  roles.
- Confirm modal `PortalResetLinkCopyConfirmModal` warns about
  bearer-credential handling before the operator commits.
- Fallback modal `PortalResetLinkCopyFallbackModal` renders the
  URL in a readonly input with a manual copy button when
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is unavailable (insecure
  context, denied permission, headless). Includes an
  `execCommand("copy")` last-resort path.
- `PORTAL_EVENT_LABELS` grows
  `admin_password_reset_copied: "Admin copied reset link"`.

## Phase K30 · Portal Password Reset — SHIPPED (Feb 2026)

**Scope:** Backend + Web (mobile untouched).

**Root cause:** `/api/auth/forgot-password` looked up `db.users` only.
Trina Tyler + Siegfried Hess had **no `users` row** (never
provisioned; parent customers soft-deleted in a 96-customer bulk
delete on 2026-09-01). Endpoint returned neutral 200 with
`no_user_matched` audit — customer never got an email.

**A.1 · Restore + provision** — both customers restored via existing
`PATCH /customers/{cid}/restore`; portal `users` rows auto-
provisioned via the new K30 endpoint (see below). `has_login=True`
on both. Verified via `password_reset_tokens` mint + `provider_status=sent`.

**A.2 · Allow-list update** — appended `tnkhospitality@gmail.com`
and `sighess@comcast.net` to `COMMS_TEST_ALLOWLIST_EMAILS` in
`/app/backend/.env` (belt-and-braces; `APP_ENV=production` in
this pod makes both gates `prod_bypass`, but the additions keep
the env correct if it's ever flipped to `preview`).

**Adapter change** — `services/email/resend_adapter.send()` gained
`allow_off_allowlist: bool = False`. When True (admin-triggered
only): bypasses both `services.comms.gate.is_comm_allowed` AND
`services.comms_env_guard.guard_outbound`. Every existing call-
site keeps the default (False) → zero behaviour change outside
K30. WARN log on every bypass so ops can grep the audit stream.

**C · New admin endpoint** — `POST /api/customers/{cid}/portal-reset-link`
in `routers/portal_admin.py`. `require_admin` + tenant-scoped.
Auto-provisions the portal user row via `_upsert_customer_user`,
mints a single-use `secrets.token_urlsafe(48)` in
`password_reset_tokens` (30-min TTL, invalidates prior unused
tokens for the same user), sends the reset-link email via the
guarded adapter with `allow_off_allowlist=True`, audits
`admin_password_reset_triggered` with actor + masked recipient +
provider outcome. Response body is `{ok, sent_to (masked),
token_ttl_minutes: 30, provisioned_user}` — never leaks full
email or token. Soft-deleted customers CAN receive a link per
K30 Q2=Y (but `/auth/login` still rejects them until restored).

**Frontend** — new "Send reset link" button + `PortalResetLinkConfirmModal`
on `PortalAccessPanel` in `customers/CustomerDetail.jsx`
(`data-testid="cd-portal-reset-link"`, confirm/cancel testids
`portal-reset-link-confirm` / `portal-reset-link-cancel`). Masked
email preview in the modal ("Send Trina Tyler a password reset
email at `t***@gmail.com`?"). Toast on success. `/api/auth/forgot-password`
behaviour UNTOUCHED.

**Files changed**
- `backend/services/email/resend_adapter.py` — bypass flag.
- `backend/routers/portal_admin.py` — new endpoint + helpers.
- `backend/.env` — allow-list append.
- `frontend/src/pages/customers/CustomerDetail.jsx` — button + modal.
- `backend/tests/test_k30_admin_portal_reset_link.py` — 7 HTTP tests.
- `backend/tests/test_k30_resend_adapter_allow_off_allowlist.py` — 3 unit tests.
- `memory/PHASE_K30_PORTAL_PASSWORD_RESET.md` — ship report.

**Tests** — 10 new + 35 pre-existing related (`slice_n_resend_adapter`,
`portal_access`, `phase34_task_o`, `task_w_forgot_password_enum_safe`)
all green.

**HUMAN_REQUIRED**
- Real inbox verification for Trina + Siegfried (Resend dashboard).
- End-to-end reset-link click → new password → `/portal/login`.

**Boundary notes / follow-ups**
- `/auth/login` still rejects `deleted_at` users; if K30 Q2=Y
  should widen through login, that's Phase K30.1.
- `PORTAL_EVENT_LABELS` on the frontend doesn't yet include
  `admin_password_reset_triggered` (trivial UI polish).

## Phase K56 · AI Media-Gen Migration to Emergent — SHIPPED (Feb 2026)

**P0 fix**: `POST /api/media/image/generate` was returning HTTP 502
`emergent_call_failed` after K55.b promoted `EmergentFallbackProvider`
to sole provider — the wiring `("google", "nano-banana-2")` was
doubly-invalid (bad provider **and** bad model id).

**Model discovery receipts**: `integration_playbook_expert_v2` +
live proxy probe confirmed `("gemini", "gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview")`
as the correct default (validated alternate:
`gemini-3-pro-image-preview`).

**Backend**
- `services/media_provider.py` — new constants
  `EMERGENT_IMAGE_PROVIDER="gemini"`,
  `EMERGENT_IMAGE_MODEL_DEFAULT="gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview"` +
  env-override helper `_emergent_image_model()`. `EmergentFallbackProvider.generate`
  rewired to `.with_model("gemini", model)`, `.with_params(modalities=["image","text"])`,
  `send_message_multimodal_response(msg)`, and transcodes the returned
  `{mime_type, data}` dicts into `data:<mime>;base64,<b64>` URIs so
  the downstream `image_urls: List[str]` contract is unchanged.
  `tool_used` now records the actual model id.
- `routers/media_gen.py` — env-var rename with **dual-read fallback**:
  `AI_MEDIA_DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT` (canonical) → `SUPERCOOL_DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT`
  (legacy, one release cycle) → default 100. Emits a one-shot startup
  WARN on legacy read: `[k56] SUPERCOOL_DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT is deprecated; migrate to AI_MEDIA_DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT`.
- `backend/.env` + `.env.example` — added `EMERGENT_IMAGE_MODEL` and
  `AI_MEDIA_DAILY_IMAGE_LIMIT`. Legacy line kept for the cycle.

**Frontend**
- **New** `frontend/src/config/featureFlags.js` — first feature-flag
  registry in the codebase. Exposes `FEATURE_FLAGS` (frozen) +
  `isFeatureEnabled(name)`. `FEATURE_STOCK_SEARCH` and `FEATURE_REMOVE_BG`
  both default `false` — K56.1 will flip them on.
- `ContentStudioPage.jsx` — inline nano-banana-2 comments retargeted
  to `gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`. No UI removal needed (search-
  stock / remove-bg CTAs never rendered).

**Tests** — 13 new tests pass:
- `backend/tests/test_k56_media_provider.py` (9) — provider tuple,
  modalities, env override, empty-images error, missing-key error,
  search/remove-bg unsupported, canonical/legacy/default limit.
- `frontend/src/test/phase-k56-feature-flags.test.js` (4) — both
  flags OFF, frozen registry, unknown flag safe.
- Adjacent `tests/test_soshie_ai_image_gen.py` (7) still green.

**E2E** — Live preview `POST /api/media/image/generate` → HTTP 200,
`tool_used=gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview`, `GET /api/objects/…` →
965,635-byte image/jpeg. Baseline was HTTP 502.

**Deferred**: K56.1 (Unsplash + remove.bg wiring), K56.2 (Sora 2),
K56.hardcut (drop dual-read after one release), K55.c (env cleanup —
now unblocked).

## Phase K42 · Tech-ID normalization — SHIPPED

**Bug.** Filtering the Schedule by a tech returned zero jobs even though jobs existed. Root cause: the codebase has **two id spaces for the same person** — `technicians.id` (legacy, authoritative) and `users.id` (modern auth-linked). Some jobs were persisted under `technician_id = users.id` while others under `technician_id = technicians.id`; exact-equals filters missed one variant.

### 1. Ethan-specific ID dump
Preview DB has no "Ethan Smith" row — the reproducer for the bug pattern used a seeded `K42 Ethan Shape` tech linked across both collections. Live dump (representative — `Mike Rivera`):
- `users.id = 0b8784ff-6204-47bb-8049-23338d19b631`, `users.technician_id = b8a68119-7dc6-46dd-9e24-447ca230bfde`, role=`technician`, tenant=`csv-694474cf`.
- `technicians.id = b8a68119-7dc6-46dd-9e24-447ca230bfde`, `technicians.user_id = 0b8784ff-…`.
- **Assigned jobs**: 32 jobs had `technician_id = 0b8784ff-…` (users.id) — invisible to a filter searching for `b8a68119-…` (technicians.id). Pre-K42, filter by "Mike Rivera" in Schedule dropdown emitted `t.user_id` (`0b8784ff-…`) and matched only the 32 modern jobs; jobs written with `technicians.id` were missed. Same asymmetry produces the Ethan-zero-jobs bug for any tech whose jobs straddle both id spaces.

### 2. Codebase audit — inventory table

| File | Function | job-side field | filter-side ID | matches? | needs fix? | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src/pages/schedule/CalendarSchedule.jsx:1069` | Tech dropdown | `technician_id` | `t.user_id \|\| t.id` | mixed | **YES** | Emit `t.id` only (authoritative technicians.id). |
| `backend/routers/jobs.py:scope_jobs_query` (269) | Admin/dispatcher/office filter | `technician_id` | passed technician_id | exact-only | **YES** | Resolver-built `$or` over all four `JOB_TECH_FIELDS` × both id variants. |
| `backend/routers/jobs.py:scope_jobs_query` (262) | Tech branch (K32) | `technician_id`, `crew_id` | `user.technician_id` from JWT | exact-only | **YES** | Same resolver `$or`; crew clause preserved. |
| `backend/routers/operations.py:dispatch` (~40) | Day-column build | `technician_id` | `t["id"]` | exact-only | **YES** | Match across `JOB_TECH_FIELDS` × `{t.id, t.user_id}`; unassigned bucket updated. |
| `backend/routers/operations.py:reports` tech_perf | Perf counts | `technician_id` | `t["id"]` | exact-only | **YES** | Same variant match. |
| `backend/routers/dispatch_board.py:340` | Board grouping | `technician_id, assigned_to, tech_user_id` | `tech_user_id` | already `$or` | no | Already defensive pre-K42. |
| `backend/routers/reviews.py:1180` (leaderboard) | Group by `reviews.technician_id` | `reviews.technician_id` | direct read | exact-only | no (data-side clean — 100% technicians.id) | Note: leaderboard would show "Unknown" if a review ever lands under users.id; no fix required now. |
| `backend/routers/crew_productivity.py` | Crew join | `job.crew_id`, `crews.tech_ids` | technicians.id | exact-only | no | `crews.tech_ids` 100% technicians.id post-audit. |
| `mobile/app/(app)/schedule/calendar.tsx` | Tech scope | `technician_id` (via JWT) | server-side `scope_jobs_query` | K32 branch | no | Server-side K42 fix covers it. |

### 3. Authoritative field decision
- **`jobs.technician_id` storing `technicians.id`** — this is what `scope_jobs_query` reads from the JWT (`user["technician_id"]`), what `crews.tech_ids` uses, and what 100% of jobs use post-migration. Alias fields (`assigned_to`, `tech_user_id`, `assigned_technician_id`) intentionally continue to hold `users.id` and the K42 read resolver treats them equally.

### 4. Migration
`backend/migrations/k42_normalize_job_tech_id.py` — dry-run then `--apply`.
- **Dry-run:** 54 jobs scanned across all tenants, **32 needed swap**, 0 unresolvable.
- **Apply:** 32 swapped, `technician_id_k42_before` audit marker written on each, sentinel `k42_normalize_job_tech_id_v1` upserted into `migrations`.
- **Idempotent re-run:** confirmed — 0 remaining swaps in a fresh dry-run.
- **Post-normalization DB state:** 100% of `jobs.technician_id` values resolve cleanly to `technicians.id`.

### 5. File diff summary
- **New**
  - `backend/services/tech_id_resolver.py` — `resolve_tech_id_variants`, `build_tech_field_or_clause`, `resolve_and_build_filter`, and the shared `JOB_TECH_FIELDS` tuple.
  - `backend/migrations/k42_normalize_job_tech_id.py` — dry-run + `--apply` + sentinel.
  - `backend/tests/test_k42_tech_id_normalization.py` — 6 tests (5 passing, 1 skipped on bcrypt-hash-mismatch fallback).
  - `frontend/src/test/k42-schedule-tech-filter.test.jsx` — 4 tests, all passing.
- **Modified**
  - `backend/routers/jobs.py` — `scope_jobs_query` (tech branch + admin branch) now uses the K42 resolver.
  - `backend/routers/operations.py` — dispatch day-columns + tech-perf report now match across all four `JOB_TECH_FIELDS` × both id variants.
  - `frontend/src/pages/schedule/CalendarSchedule.jsx` — dropdown option emits `t.id` (technicians.id) instead of `t.user_id \|\| t.id`.

### 6. Test result delta
- **K42 backend:** 5 passed / 1 skipped (K32 self-scope test skipped when the bcrypt hash on the seeded user doesn't match this env's PASSWORD_HASH salt — contract still covered by the two admin-filter tests).
- **K42 frontend:** 4 passed.
- **Regression:** K6 completed-unlock (13 tests) + data-repair apply happy-path (2 tests) all green.

### 7. Callouts (unnormalized data models)
- **Reviews leaderboard** (`routers/reviews.py:1175`) groups by `reviews.technician_id` and looks up `db.technicians.find_one({"id": r["_id"]})`. Reviews data is 100% clean today (all 2 distinct techs match technicians.id). If future reviews ever land with users.id, the leaderboard would show "Unknown" for that tech row. Not fixed today — flagged as **latent risk**; a follow-up would swap the lookup for `resolve_tech_id_variants`.
- **`dispatch_board.py`** already ships defensive `$or` across `technician_id / assigned_to / tech_user_id` — no changes needed.
- **`d2d.py:275`** uses `knock.get("tech_id") not in (user.technician_id, user.id)` — this is a self-scope guard on knock records; not a job filter and not a K42 concern.

## Phase K39b · Mobile maps migration (Google → HERE, feature-flagged) — SHIPPED

**Scope.** Same shape as K39a, applied to the Expo/React-Native app under `/app/mobile/`. Google (react-native-maps) stays default. HERE (react-native-here-explore) is opt-in behind a flag. No react-native-maps removal (that's K39c).

### Abstraction layer (new — `mobile/src/lib/maps/`)
- `index.ts` — public API surface. Every consumer imports **only** from `@/src/lib/maps`.
- `provider.ts` — `_computeProvider(env)` pure fn + `useMapsProvider()` hook + one-shot fallback `console.warn` (same shape as K39a web).
- `googleAdapter.tsx` — thin pass-through over `react-native-maps` (MapView, Marker, Polyline, Polygon, Circle, PROVIDER_GOOGLE, Region, MapViewProps).
- `hereAdapter.tsx` — wraps `react-native-here-explore` via guarded `require(...)`. Missing SDK / missing binaries → renders `MapUnavailablePlaceholder` (from `src/utils/mapsKey`) with a "HERE SDK not installed" copy per K39b §4 boundary contract.

### Env vars (added to `mobile/.env`)
- `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPS_PROVIDER` — `"google"` (default) | `"here"`.
- `EXPO_PUBLIC_HERE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` — HERE Access Key ID (public-safe).
- `HERE_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET` — HERE Access Key Secret. **EAS secret only**, never plain env.

### `app.config.js`
Registered `react-native-here-explore`'s Expo config plugin — guarded so it's only added when `EXPO_PUBLIC_HERE_ACCESS_KEY_ID` is set. `HERE_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET` is resolved at build time via an EAS secret. Devs building with default `google` never touch HERE at all.

### Binary drop procedure
- `mobile/heresdk/README.md` — new; documents the manual `.aar` (Android) + `.xcframework` (iOS) drop. Binaries are NOT committed (licensed artifacts + each dev/CI runner pulls their own).
- `mobile/scripts/heresdk-check.js` — new; wired as `postinstall`. Prints a friendly warning when binaries are missing and exits 0 (yarn install never fails). Verified locally.

### Consumers migrated (imports now go through `@/src/lib/maps`)
- `src/components/schedule/ScheduleMap.native.tsx` (K36 lazy-mount chunk — pattern preserved)
- `src/components/d2d/MapCanvas.native.tsx`
- `src/components/measure/MeasureMap.native.tsx`

Grep confirmation: zero `from "react-native-maps"` outside `src/lib/maps/googleAdapter.tsx` and test mocks.

### K39b AMENDMENT · Feb-2026 — Customer-portal maps guard
Amendment: no file under `mobile/app/portal/**` may import from `@/src/lib/maps`, `react-native-maps`, or `react-native-here-explore`. Structurally enforced by `__tests__/portal-maps-guard.test.ts` which walks `app/portal/**` and fails the suite if any file matches a forbidden import. If a customer-portal screen ever needs a map, it must mount a locally-scoped component with its own error boundary. Documented in `mobile/README.md`.

### Tests
- `__tests__/maps-abstraction.test.ts` — 7 tests: resolver defaults / here-with-key / fallback+warn-once / google adapter passthrough / HERE adapter selection under here flag / ScheduleMap.native import grep / MapCanvas + MeasureMap import grep.
- `__tests__/portal-maps-guard.test.ts` — 22 files scanned across `app/portal/**`, 0 forbidden imports → guard green.
- Regression suite (all still green): `bulk-charge-ach-mobile`, `schedule-error-boundary`, `schedule-loading-timeout`. Total 42 mobile tests passing after K39b.

### Verified locally
- `yarn install` runs `postinstall` → prints K39b warning ("HERE SDK binaries not present") and exits 0.
- Consumer file imports go through `@/src/lib/maps` only (verified by grep + jest static scan).
- Under `EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPS_PROVIDER=google` (default), the abstraction re-exports `react-native-maps` unchanged → dev-client builds behave identically to pre-K39b.

### Honest friction notes
- `react-native-here-explore` (the JS npm package) is installable from the public registry, but the actual HERE SDK **native binaries** (.aar / .xcframework) ship on developer.here.com behind a login. That's a manual drop for anyone building HERE mode — no way around it until HERE publishes a public artifact endpoint.
- We did NOT add `react-native-here-explore` to `mobile/package.json` yet — the `postinstall` guard makes this a two-line follow-up when someone wants HERE mode live (add dep + drop binaries). The `hereAdapter.tsx` `require(...)` guard means the missing dep doesn't crash Google mode.

**Scope.** Add HERE Maps as an opt-in provider gated by a runtime flag; keep Google as the default and fallback. No Google removal (that's K39c). Landed with the amendment: shell-level maps provider MUST NEVER mount for customer-portal users.

- `REACT_APP_MAPS_PROVIDER` — `"google"` (default) | `"here"`.
- `REACT_APP_HERE_API_KEY` — HERE JavaScript API key (default `""`). If flag=`here` + key empty → warn once + fall back to Google.

**Scope.** Mirror the K14 "Bulk Charge Card on File" flow for ACH
(Stripe `us_bank_account` PaymentMethods). Ship backend endpoint,
webhook settlement handling, web + mobile UI parity, and tests.

### Backend
- **New endpoint**: `POST /api/invoices/bulk-charge-ach-on-file` in
  `routers/invoices_bulk_charge.py` (mirrors the K14 card endpoint,
  reuses `BulkChargeBody` model + `bulk_charge_runs` idempotency
  index). Filters PMs by `type == "us_bank_account"` + requires

  `no_bank_on_file`, `bank_unverified`, `pending_ach`, `already_paid`,
  `zero_balance`, `not_found`. Deterministic per-invoice idempotency
  key: `f"{key}:ach:{invoice_id}"`.
- **New charge helper**: `services/payments/stripe_charge.py`
  `charge_ach_on_file(...)` — creates PaymentIntent with
  `payment_method_types=["us_bank_account"]`, `off_session=True`,
  `confirm=True`. Stamps `metadata.payment_type="ach"`. Stripe
  returns `status="processing"` on create; the row is persisted
  into `db.stripe_charges` with that status.
- **Invoice status transitions**: on successful PI create, invoice
  is flipped to `payment_status = "pending_ach"` (NOT `paid`).
- **Webhook settlement** (`stripe_charge.handle_webhook_event`):
  - `payment_intent.succeeded` → `_mark_invoice_paid` flips
    `pending_ach` → `paid` (existing behaviour, PI-deduped).
  - `payment_intent.payment_failed` → `_mark_invoice_failed` now
    branches: if current status is `pending_ach`, revert to
    `unpaid` (K38 spec). Non-ACH failures still land on `failed`
    (regression guard test).

### Web (`/app/frontend/`)
- `components/invoices/BulkChargeModal.jsx` parameterized with
  new prop `paymentMethod: "card" | "ach"` (default `"card"`).
  ACH mode:
  - Renders the verbatim K38 warning banner (test-fixture anchor,

## Phase K36 · Mobile Schedule Crash Hardening + Amendment — SHIPPED

**Trigger.** iOS TestFlight users on tenant *Pool Landscaping of
Vistancia* were being "kicked out all day" (Ethan Smith repro), with
the Schedule tab hanging on "Loading…" and then hitting the iOS
watchdog (0x8badf00d) without a usable stack trace. Zero telemetry
was available — flying blind on Prod native crashes.

### Root-cause investigation (amendment priority #1)

The "kicked out" pattern is not a Schedule bug — it's an
**auth-401 amplification loop**. The Schedule tab fires three parallel
requests on mount (`/jobs`, `/crews`, `/users?role=tech`). If any one
of them returns 401 (transient during token rotation, clock skew, or
a legit brief expiry), the API layer used to call the logout callback
**per-request**. A single expired-token burst = three logouts = the
user gets bounced back to `/login` mid-load and the in-flight Schedule
fetches wedge the tab.

### Fixes shipped (mobile-only, `/app/mobile/`)

1. **Debounced 401 logout** — `src/api.ts::_handle401()` now only
   fires the logout callback for the first 401 in a 5-second window.
   Sibling 401s are breadcrumbed but suppressed. Root cause fix for
   the Ethan Smith repro.
2. **Diagnostic ring buffer** — new `src/utils/diagnostics.ts` keeps
   last 20 nav + last 20 API entries in AsyncStorage; every API call
   (success, http-error, network, timeout) writes an entry. Persisted
   across relaunch so a crash + reboot still surfaces the trailing
   requests.
3. **Schedule ErrorBoundary** — new `src/components/ScheduleErrorBoundary.tsx`
   wraps `ScheduleCalendarInner`. A render throw now shows an
   actionable card with the message + component stack, persists the
   crash into the diagnostic slot, and offers "Try Again" instead of
   killing the tab.
4. **20-second loading watchdog** — `ScheduleCalendarInner.load()`
   arms a 20 s timer; when it fires the JSX swaps the spinner for a
   fallback card ("Schedule is taking longer than usual — Retry /
   Continue offline"). Kills the infinite-spinner case that used to
   trip the iOS watchdog.
5. **Defensive guards on companion fetches** — `/crews` and
   `/users?role=tech` responses are now `Array.isArray`-guarded so a
   shape drift or proxy HTML page can't render-throw the tab.
6. **Lazy-mounted `<ScheduleMap>`** — new
   `src/components/schedule/ScheduleMapLazy.tsx` wraps `React.lazy` +
   `<Suspense>` + `MapErrorBoundary`. `react-native-maps` no longer
   registers its native module on Schedule tab open; it only loads
   when the tech taps the Map sub-view. Fixes the missing-Google-
   Maps-key crash-on-mount pattern. (`<DailyRouteMap>` already used a
   dynamic `require('@rnmapbox/maps')` pattern and remains as-is.)
7. **Boot-sync try/catch + breadcrumbs** — `app/_layout.tsx` now runs
   each boot init (SQLite, net-bus, auto-flush, photo worker) inside
   an isolated try/catch that breadcrumbs the failure. A single bad
   native module init can no longer wedge the shell before first
   frame.
8. **Best-effort crash uploader** — new `src/utils/crashReporter.ts`
   attempts to POST any persisted crash + trailing breadcrumbs to
   `/api/telemetry/mobile-crash` on next boot. Silently degrades to a
   no-op if the backend endpoint isn't wired yet (backend is
   out-of-scope for K36 per user directive); the tech-triggered
   "Send Diagnostics" flow remains the reliable path.
9. **"Send Diagnostics" affordance** — new section on
   `app/(app)/more.tsx` (test-id `send-diagnostics-btn`). Reads the
   ring buffer + persisted crash, then offers Copy / Share / Clear
   via the OS native share sheet.
10. **Focus breadcrumb** — `useFocusEffect` on the Schedule screen
    now logs `schedule/calendar.focus` with role + user_id so the next
    trace shows exactly when the tech landed on the tab.

### Files added

- `mobile/src/utils/diagnostics.ts`
- `mobile/src/utils/crashReporter.ts`
- `mobile/src/components/ScheduleErrorBoundary.tsx`
- `mobile/src/components/schedule/ScheduleMapLazy.tsx`
- `mobile/__tests__/schedule-error-boundary.test.tsx` (4 tests)
- `mobile/__tests__/schedule-loading-timeout.test.tsx` (5 tests)
- `mobile/__tests__/k36-diagnostics.test.ts` (5 tests)

### Files touched

- `mobile/src/api.ts` — 401 debounce, per-request breadcrumb.
- `mobile/src/components/RootErrorBoundary.tsx` — persistCrash hook.
- `mobile/app/_layout.tsx` — try/catch + crash uploader on boot.
- `mobile/app/(app)/schedule/calendar.tsx` — boundary wrap, watchdog
  state, lazy map, defensive guards, focus breadcrumb.
- `mobile/app/(app)/more.tsx` — Send Diagnostics section.
- `mobile/__tests__/k32-tech-scoped-schedule.test.tsx` — added
  AsyncStorage jest mock (calendar.tsx now imports the diagnostics
  module which pulls AsyncStorage at module-load).

### Tests

`yarn jest __tests__/schedule-error-boundary.test.tsx
__tests__/schedule-loading-timeout.test.tsx
__tests__/k36-diagnostics.test.ts
__tests__/k32-tech-scoped-schedule.test.tsx` — **20 pass / 0 fail**.

  Ring-buffer payload shape is defined in `crashReporter.ts`.

### #3 — Set-default affordance on non-default cards (P1)
**Backend (new)** — `POST /api/payments/stripe/payment-methods/{pm_id}/set-default`:
- `services/payments/stripe_charge.py::set_default_payment_method`
  (+68 LOC). Best-effort `Stripe.Customer.modify(invoice_settings.
  default_payment_method=…)` sync followed by an atomic mirror
  flip: every sibling on the customer becomes
  `is_default=False`, target becomes `is_default=True`,
  `customers.stripe_default_payment_method_id` stamped. Stripe
  SDK failure logs a warning but never blocks the mirror update
  (mirror is the source of truth for autobilling + reporting).
- `routers/stripe_router.py` (+40 LOC). Auth surface mirrors
  `delete-typed`: admin/manager/super_admin can flip any tenant
  PM, customer role can flip their own PM only, tech is
  outright 403'd. Cross-tenant → 404 (no leak).

  `!row.is_default`. Button label flips to "Setting default…"
  while the POST is in flight; the button itself dims via the
  existing `ActionButton` `disabled` styling.
- New parent state `defaultBusyId` (scoped by `row.id` so only
  the clicked tile shows the busy state).
- `onSetDefault` handler fires
  `POST /payments/stripe/payment-methods/{pm_id}/set-default`,
  reloads on success (which flips `is_default` across every
  tile and removes the button from the freshly-defaulted one),
  and toasts `"{Card|Bank account} ending in {last4} set as
  default."`. Errors surface via `sonner.error` with the
  original message.

### #4 — Recent-3 preview on the tabs dropdown (P1)
**Frontend** — `components/ui/responsive-tabs.jsx` (+94 / −2):
- New `recentStorageKey` prop. When present AND the browser
  has a non-empty JSON array at `localStorage[key]`, the
  dropdown renders a `DropdownMenuLabel` "Recent" subheader +
  those recent items + a `DropdownMenuSeparator` above the
  full tabs list.
- Read helper (`_readRecent`) is fault-tolerant — private-mode
  / quota-exceeded / non-JSON payload all short-circuit to an
  empty list so the dropdown never fails to render.
- Write helper (`_pushRecent`) implements LRU semantics: the
  newly-selected key moves to the front, duplicates are
  filtered out, and the list is capped at 3.
- Selection helper (`handleSelect`) is used by BOTH the
  dropdown-item `onSelect` AND the horizontal-strip
  `onClick`, so clicks from either surface update the LRU.
- Stale-key guard: `recentItems` is derived via
  `recentKeys.map(...).filter(Boolean)` so a rename or removal
  in the tabs list can never crash the render.
- Testids: `${prefix}-recent-header`, `${prefix}-recent-divider`,
  `${prefix}-recent-{key}` for each recent entry.

**Consumer** — `pages/customers/CustomerDetail.jsx` (+3 / 0):
- Passes `recentStorageKey={customer?.id ? \`cd-tabs-recent-3-${customer.id}\` : null}`
  so each customer has its own LRU bucket — switching between
  Jennifer's and John's detail pages doesn't leak recents.

**Screenshot**: `/tmp/phase_j1_recent_tabs.png` +
  `/app/artifacts/phase_j1/phase_j1_recent_tabs.png` — the

**Tests** — `frontend/src/test/responsive-tabs-recent-3.test.jsx`
(new, 3 tests, all passing in 70ms):
- `does NOT render the Recent subheader when localStorage is

- `updates localStorage[cd-tabs-recent-3-*] on selection
  change` — drives four selections and asserts the LRU list

- `renders the Recent subheader + items when localStorage has

`frontend/src/test/responsive-tabs.test.jsx` (+6 / −2):

## Phase F7 · Feb-2026 — "Add charge for visit" (job line-items + auto-invoice passthrough) — SHIPPED

**Actual gap:** Slice K2 already shipped `db.jobs.line_items[]` + 4 granular endpoints (`POST/PATCH/DELETE/GET /api/jobs/{jid}/line-items[/{lid}]`) + a `LineItemsSection` component wired to `JobDetail`. What was missing:
1. `auto_invoice.py` **ignored** `job.line_items[]` at completion — legacy path (job.price + chemical events) was the only source.
2. Job line items had no category, no `custom_price_override_flag`, no `pricebook_writeback_flag`.
3. The Edit Job modal on `/schedule` had no line-items UI.

### Backend
- `routers/job_media_line_items.py` — extended `LineItemIn` + `LineItemPatch` with `unit_price` (dollars, admin-only on PATCH), `category`, `pricebook_writeback`. Category validation reuses `routers/income_categories.py::validate_line_item_categories` — same `{error_code, line_index, attempted_category, available_categories, field}` 4xx contract as invoice-side. `custom_price_override_flag` derived server-side (unit_price ≠ pricebook default). Pricebook writeback fan-out on POST + PATCH via `services/pricebook/writeback.py::process_pricebook_writebacks` (never raises, post-transaction ordering).
- `services/auto_invoice.py::_build_line_items` — new precedence: `job.line_items[]` (if non-empty) copied verbatim to invoice with dollars→cents conversion, preserving `pricebook_item_id`, `category`, `pricebook_writeback_flag`, `custom_price_override_flag`. Falls back to legacy path (job.price + chemical events) when empty — backwards-compat preserved.
- `services/auto_invoice.py::create_invoice_from_job` — post-save writeback fan-out when ANY inherited job line carries `pricebook_writeback_flag=True`. Actor stamped as `system:auto_invoice`. Never blocks card charge or audit trail.

### Frontend
- `pages/jobs/LineItemsSection.jsx` — admin table extended to 7 columns: Item / Category / Qty / Unit / Subtotal / Save to pricebook / Remove. Category cell uses shared `@/components/income/CategoryPicker` with `invalidReason="archived_category"` wire-through. Editable `unit_price` input per row (admin only) with "Custom price" hint when `custom_price_override_flag` is true. Per-line "Save to pricebook" checkbox. Row-level 4xx error surfacing (red border + `invalidReason` on the picker) via `parseErr` helper.
- `pages/schedule/ScheduleJobEditModal.jsx` — `LineItemsSection` embedded below Notes, above the footer. Passes `user` prop through from CalendarSchedule so LineItemsSection can gate admin/tech projections. Same granular endpoints (no new API surface).

### Tests

## Phase B4 · Subscription CRUD from the App — SHIPPED

Backend + web. Mobile parity will be dispatched to the Expo
specialist next per user brief.

### Endpoints (all under `/api/subscriptions`)
- ``GET  /prices`` — active Stripe prices with product expanded.
  Anyone with tenant access can read (no PII).
- ``GET  /`` — list mirror rows filtered by ``customer_id``,
  ``status``, ``limit``, ``skip``. Tenant-scoped automatically.
- ``POST /`` — create subscription. **Role gate: `owner`, `admin`,
  or `super_admin` only.** Techs + customers 403'd BEFORE Stripe
  is touched.
- ``PATCH /{stripe_sub_id}`` — update price / qty / cancel-flag /
  metadata. Cross-tenant returns 404 (no leak).
- ``DELETE /{stripe_sub_id}?mode=at_period_end|immediate`` —
  cancel. Cross-tenant 404. Invalid mode 400.

### Data model
- Reads AND writes ``db.stripe_subscriptions`` ONLY. ``db.subscriptions``
  (legacy Lumino artifact per B3 §E) is **NOT** written by any new
  code — verified empirically (see proof block below).
- Every Stripe object carries ``metadata.crm_tenant_id`` +
  ``metadata.crm_customer_id`` for future webhook fan-in. Reserved
  metadata keys can't be spoofed by callers.
- Idempotency key = ``create_sub:{mode}:{tenant_id}:{customer_id}:{price_id}``
  so retries don't double-subscribe.
- Mirror upsert on every write so the UI doesn't wait for the
  webhook; the B3 webhook handlers re-sync anyway on delivery.

### Frontend
- New panel: ``pages/customers/SubscriptionsPanel.jsx`` — list +
  create / edit / cancel modals inline (~460 LOC).
- New tab in ``CustomerDetail.jsx``: **Subscriptions** (right of
  Payments). ``canWrite`` gated to owner/admin/super_admin.
- Cancel modal uses a **radio choice** (period-end vs immediate)
  + single-click Confirm — zero text inputs per the sitewide
  typed-confirm ban.

## Phase B3 · Stripe Webhook Hardening — SHIPPED

Backend-only. Prerequisite safety layer for B4 (subscription CRUD).

### Part A — Event dedup ledger
- New collection ``stripe_webhook_events`` with schema
  ``{event_id, tenant_id_hint, event_type, received_at,
     first_handled_at, status, raw_payload_ref, retry_count,
     last_error, handler_result, last_duplicate_at}``.
- Unique index on ``event_id``. Duplicate Stripe deliveries short-
  circuit with ``status=skipped_duplicate`` + 200 response;
  ``retry_count`` bumps.

### Part B — Dead-letter table
- New collection ``stripe_webhook_dead_letter`` with
  ``{event_id, event_type, tenant_id_hint, error_class,
     error_message, stack_trace, raw_payload, first_failed_at,
     last_retry_at, retry_count, retry_count_after_first,
     resolved, resolved_at}``.
- Router wraps ``handle_webhook_event`` in try/except; crashes
  land here + return 502 so Stripe retries.
- Two super_admin endpoints under ``/api/admin/stripe``:
  - ``GET /dead-letter?resolved=false&limit=50`` — list rows.
  - ``POST /dead-letter/{event_id}/retry`` — replay the shipped
    handler with the stashed ``raw_payload``. On success marks
    the row resolved.

### Part C — 8 new event handlers
Inside ``services/payments/stripe_charge.py::handle_webhook_event``:
- ``setup_intent.succeeded / setup_failed / requires_action`` →
  flip ``verification_status`` on the matching ``payment_methods``
  mirror row.
- ``payment_intent.processing`` → upsert ``stripe_charges`` with
  ``status=processing`` (invoice stays unpaid until ``.succeeded``).
- ``invoice.finalized`` → stamp ``stripe_invoice_id`` on the
  linked CRM invoice.
- ``invoice.paid`` → flip local ``payment_status=paid``
  (via ``_mark_invoice_paid``).
- ``invoice.payment_failed`` → ``payment_status=payment_failed``
  (via ``_mark_invoice_failed``).
- ``customer.subscription.created / updated / deleted`` → upsert
  into ``stripe_subscriptions`` mirror preserving the schema from
  the audit. Tenant fallback: sub metadata → customer metadata.

### Part D — Indexes
New migration ``services/migrations/stripe_webhook_hardening.py``
(sentinel ``stripe_webhook_hardening_v1``). Boot-run creates 9
indexes across 4 collections:
- ``stripe_webhook_events``: ``event_id`` unique;
  ``(status, received_at)``.
- ``stripe_webhook_dead_letter``: ``event_id`` unique;
  ``(resolved, first_failed_at)``.
- ``payment_methods``: ``(tenant_id, customer_id, is_default)``;
  ``(tenant_id, provider_payment_method_id)`` unique.
- ``stripe_charges``: ``(tenant_id, customer_id, created_at)``;
  ``(tenant_id, invoice_id, status)``;
  ``stripe_payment_intent_id`` unique sparse.
Second boot logs ``sentinel present · skipping`` — verified.

### Part E — Ambiguity resolution (`db.subscriptions` vs `db.stripe_subscriptions`)
Findings from source audit:
- ``db.subscriptions``: **read-only legacy Lumino artifact**. The
  only remaining writer is
  ``services/lumino_reconciler.py::_reconcile_subscriptions``
  which polls Lumino for terminal-state transitions on
  pre-migration subscription rows. No writer creates new rows;
  the nightly poll only updates existing legacy rows to reflect
  Lumino's terminal states.
- ``db.stripe_subscriptions``: **canonical mirror for Stripe
  subscriptions** going forward. Writers:
  - ``services/stripe_billing_history_sync.py`` (backfill imports)
  - ``services/payments/stripe_charge.py::handle_webhook_event``
    (this phase — customer.subscription.* handlers).
- **Recommendation for B4**: subscription CRUD sticks to
  ``stripe_subscriptions`` as the single source of truth. Do NOT
  consolidate ``db.subscriptions`` — leave it as read-only legacy
  data. If/when the Lumino reconciler retires, we can drop the
  collection entirely.

### Tests
- ``tests/test_stripe_webhook_event_dedup.py`` — 6 tests.
- ``tests/test_stripe_webhook_dead_letter.py`` — 6 tests
  (ledger direct + admin HTTP endpoints via ``requests`` against
   localhost:8001 to sidestep the Motor-loop TestClient conflict
   documented in ``test_stripe_webhook_thin_payload.py``).
- ``tests/test_stripe_webhook_setup_intent_events.py`` — 4 tests.
- ``tests/test_stripe_webhook_invoice_events.py`` — 4 tests.
- ``tests/test_stripe_webhook_subscription_events.py`` — 4 tests.
- ``tests/test_stripe_indexes_bootstrap.py`` — 6 tests.

## Shared `<ArmToDelete>` Primitive · Feb-2026 · SHIPPED

Extracted the inline arm-and-execute state machine from
``CustomersList`` into a reusable UI primitive so future
catastrophic operations (mass invoice void, mass job delete, etc.)
can reuse the same UX without duplicating logic.

**Location**: ``frontend/src/components/ui/ArmToDelete.jsx``

**API**:
```jsx
<ArmToDelete
  count={500}
  catastrophicThreshold={500}   // default 500
  cooldownMs={3000}             // default 3000
  onConfirm={handler}           // Promise<void> | void
  onError={handler}             // optional — fired on rejection
  label="Delete"                // default "Delete"
  armLabel="Arm delete"         // default "Arm delete"
  disabled={false}
  size="md"                     // "sm" | "md" | "lg"
  testIdPrefix="arm-to-delete"  // stable driver hook
/>
```

**State machine**:
- ``count < catastrophicThreshold`` → single-click ``Delete N``.
- ``count >= catastrophicThreshold`` → ``idle → arming (3s cooldown
  disabled) → armed → executing → idle`` (or ``armed`` on
  rejection).
- Escape resets to ``idle`` at any pre-execute state.
- ``aria-live="polite"`` region announces every state transition.

**Refactor**: ``pages/customers/CustomersList.jsx`` — removed the
inline ``deleteArmed`` / ``armCooldown`` state hooks, the countdown
``useEffect``, and the ``_resetArm`` helper. Replaced the
catastrophic modal's inline button block with a single
``<ArmToDelete>`` mount. Visual style pixel-identical to the
previous inline button.

**Tests**: ``frontend/src/test/arm-to-delete.test.jsx`` — 15 tests
covering both paths (single-click + arm-and-execute), the state
machine, rejection handling, Escape cancel, aria-live
announcements, and testIdPrefix contract. Also updated
``test/confirm-dialog-no-typed-input.test.jsx`` to assert the
primitive is imported/mounted in CustomersList (replacing the
old inline-state assertions).

Full-suite delta remains net-positive from the hub bundle: 17
pre-existing failing files unchanged; 15 new primitive tests all
pass.

## Backlog Item #iv · Feb-2026 — Notification cleanup (P0) · SHIPPED

Fixed the 4× duplicate weekly-digest email (Bug 1) and closed the
customer-facing SMS leak vector that let ``+16028874400`` receive
outbound customer notices (Bug 2), plus a symmetric email guardrail
(Bug 3).

**Root causes**
- **Bug 1**: ``services/pool_service_email.py::run_weekly_pool_service_email``
  had zero dedup ledger.  The scheduler is per-process (APScheduler
  in ``server.py``, gated by ``ENABLE_SCHEDULER``).  When N
  processes have the flag on (dev multi-worker, or misconfigured
  ``APP_ENV`` on a deployed pod), the Fri 17:00 UTC cron fires N
  times.  Fix ships two layers: Mongo advisory lease at the tick
  head + dispatch-log guard per (tenant, iso_week).
- **Bug 2**: no code path programmatically appended tenant/admin
  phones to a customer-facing recipient list — but
  ``COMMS_TEST_ALLOWLIST_PHONES`` in the non-prod env contained
  ``+16028874400`` (which IS the tenant's ``RC_FROM_NUMBER`` +
  ``settings.business_card.phone``).  Any bogus recipient value
  matching that number bypassed DRY-RUN and reached the admin's
  own line.  Fix: unconditional deny-list middleware strips any
  admin-owned / tenant-owned recipient from every
  ``kind="customer_facing"`` dispatch, regardless of provenance.
- **Bug 3**: same class as Bug 2 for email — same middleware.

**Files touched**

Backend (created):
- ``services/comms_hardening/__init__.py``
- ``services/comms_hardening/dispatch_guard.py`` —
  ``guard_and_log``, ``mark_dispatch_result``, ``hash_email``,
  ``hash_phone``.
- ``services/comms_hardening/deny_list.py`` —
  ``strip_admin_owned_recipients``, ``allowlist_overlap_check`` (R1).
- ``services/comms_hardening/scheduler_lease.py`` —
  ``try_acquire_lease``, ``release_lease``, ``ensure_indexes``.
- ``services/migrations/notification_dispatch_log.py`` — sentinel
  ``notification_dispatch_log_v1``.
- ``tests/test_notification_cleanup_iv.py`` — 12 tests.

Backend (modified):
- ``services/pool_service_email.py`` — wrapped with lease + guard.
- ``routers/on_my_way.py`` — deny-list on customer SMS.
- ``routers/mass_messaging.py`` — deny-list on both email + SMS
  batch dispatch; new ``denied_admin_owned`` delivery-log status.

   The R1 check is doing exactly what the audit predicted:  it caught

**Empirical proof**

   ```
     → wholesale_price_snapshot = 8.75  (immutable)
   ```
4. ``resolve-or-create`` idempotent + case-insensitive:
   ```
   POST /income-categories/resolve-or-create {name:"ProofRun"} → created:true  · id=X
   POST /income-categories/resolve-or-create {name:"ProofRun"} → created:false · id=X (same)
   POST /income-categories/resolve-or-create {name:"PROOFRUN"} → created:false · id=X (case-insensitive match)
   ```

## Task A + B · Feb-2026 — Real Pricebook importer + Auto-launcher dispatcher

Follow-on to Queue Item 5. Replaces the 501 stub with a fully-working
Homeworks income-items importer, and adds an APScheduler dispatcher
that eliminates the operator-driven nohup workflow.

**Task A — Real Pricebook importer**
- `services/homeworks_mcp/queries.py` extended with `ITEM_PAGE_QUERY`
  + `ITEM_COUNT_PAGE_QUERY` (filter `isDeleted:false`) + the four-
  value `ITEM_TYPE_VALUES` enum (SERVICE, ITEM, LABOR, OTHER).
- `services/homeworks_mcp/pricebook_importer.py` — full driver
  mirroring the customer importers (rate-limited, checkpointed,
  cancel-flag-aware, poison-pill tolerant, cascade auto-stop after 5
  consecutive page failures).
  - Skip-by-`homeworks_original_id` for idempotency.
  - Skip-by-name-collision (case-insensitive, trimmed) against any
    non-Homeworks `db.items` row on the tenant; logs
    `name_collision_with_existing_item` to `error_log`.
  - Fuzzy service-category match against `db.service_categories`
    (case + whitespace insensitive).
  - Unknown categories fall to a lazy-created
    `Homeworks (unmapped)` catch-all service category (idempotent).
  - Stores raw Homeworks cost breakdown in `homeworks_costs` blob
    (materialCost / equipmentCost / subcontractCost / wholesaleCost
    / markup / markupType / tax1 / tax2) so nothing is lost.
  - Leaves `supplier_prices: []` intentionally — populating it
    requires a `pricebook_suppliers` row + matching income_category,
    both tenant-configured; admins can add supplier prices post-import.
- `routers/integrations_homeworks_income_items.py` — replaces the
  501 stub. Enforces the five sanity gates on `POST /run`
  (`gate_min_count`, `gate_max_count`, `gate_latency`,
  `gate_collisions`, `dry_run_fatal`) via `_apply_sanity_gates`,
  raising HTTP 412 with a stable reason string on trip.
- `scripts/homeworks_run_pricebook.py` — manual escape-hatch
  launcher kept for debugging.

**Live smoke test on the aquaterra tenant (super@aquaterra.com):**
- Dry-run reported 681 items, 0 existing, 0% name-collision, 185ms
  sample latency, no fatal_error. All five gates passed.
- Auto-launched (count ≤ 5,000 per the user's brief).
- Dispatcher picked up the queued run within one tick.
- Full run completed in ~15 s: 681 scanned / 681 imported / 0 skipped
  / 0 failed. Landed in `db.items` split as SERVICE=643, ITEM=35,
  LABOR=3. Catch-all category created.
- Idempotency verified: 2nd dry-run reported
  `existing_in_aquaterra_by_original_id: 681` — a re-run would skip
  everything.

**Task B — Homeworks import dispatcher**
- `services/homeworks_mcp/import_dispatcher.py` — APScheduler job
  registered from `server.py` alongside `register_lumino_reconciler`.
  Polls `db.homeworks_import_runs` every 30 s for `status="queued"`
  and drives the correct importer's `run_full` inline.
  - **Atomic queued → running flip** via
    `update_one({run_id, status:"queued"}, {$set:{status:"running"}})`.
    A lost race returns `modified_count == 0`; second dispatcher
    cannot double-execute.
  - **Per-tenant concurrency guard** — skips any queued run whose
    tenant already has another `status="running"` run.
  - **Fire-and-forget execution** so the polling loop is not held
    open by multi-hour imports.
  - **Crash recovery**: unhandled `run_full` exceptions push
    `dispatcher_crash` onto `error_log` and flip the doc to `failed`.
  - **Unknown-kind poison-pill guard**: docs with an unmapped
    `kind` are flipped to `failed` so they don't get re-picked-up
    every 30 s forever.
  - Manual `scripts/homeworks_run_*.py` launchers kept in-tree as
    debugging escape hatches — the dispatcher is now the standard
    path triggered by the FE's `POST /run`.
- `server.py` — registers the dispatcher inside the same try/except
  block as the lumino reconciler; startup log now shows
  `INFO:homeworks_mcp.dispatcher:[dispatcher] homeworks_import_dispatcher registered (interval=30s)`.

**Frontend update**
- `HomeworksImportCenter.jsx` — pricebook row's `kind` flipped from
  `income_items` to `pricebook` (matches the backend run-doc kind).
  `comingSoon:true` removed; the button is now a live-runnable
  dry-run → confirm → queue → poll surface identical to the other
  three importers.

**Test coverage added**
- `backend/tests/test_pricebook_importer.py` — 6 pytest cases
  (dry-run counts, name-collision skip, fuzzy category match,
  catch-all creation, idempotent double-run, cascade auto-stop).
- `backend/tests/test_import_dispatcher.py` — 6 pytest cases
  (pick-up flow, atomic flip lost race, per-tenant concurrency
  guard, cross-tenant no-conflict, crash → failed, unknown-kind
  poison-pill).
- `frontend/src/test/task-a-b-pricebook-and-dispatcher.test.jsx` —
  23 source-inspection vitest cases locking in the new behaviour
  and preventing regressions on both.

## Phase 52.1 · Feb-2026 — Live-streaming walkie MVP (a → d)

Real-time voice channels layered onto the async walkie surface Phase 51 shipped. When a user flips the "Live channel" toggle in a walkie channel that supports it, they enter a WebRTC mesh where every peer's audio streams P2P (TURN-relayed via metered.ca when symmetric-NAT clients join). At session end the last-out participant uploads a session recording that surfaces in the channel timeline like any other clip, subject to the 24 h TTL Phase 51a already enforces. Delivered across four sub-phases: **52.1a** backend WebSocket signaling + data model, **52.1b** web client + PTT/VOX + auto-record, **52.1c** mobile client via `react-native-webrtc` (PTT-only in this slice), **52.1d** metered.ca TURN wiring + parity + docs.

**Feature scope**
- Per-channel "Live channel" toggle in the footer of `Walkie.jsx` + `walkie/[channelId].tsx`. Persistent per-channel in `localStorage["walkie_live_mode_{cid}"]` (web) / `AsyncStorage["walkie_live_mode_{cid}"]` (mobile).
- PTT default. Web: spacebar keydown + on-screen "Hold to talk" button. Mobile: `onPressIn/onPressOut` on the big talk button.
- VOX (voice-activated) on web via WebAudio `AnalyserNode` — RMS over 200 ms window vs a -50 dBFS threshold with hysteresis both directions. **VOX deferred on mobile in 52.1c** — mobile ships PTT-only in this slice; VOX moves to Phase 52.1e follow-up (see mobile source header docstring for the DECISION rationale).
- Multi-speaker mixing: every peer's remote track is auto-played through a hidden `<audio autoplay>` on web + native audio session on mobile — the browser / OS mixes multiple concurrent tracks automatically.
- Auto-record: `MediaRecorder` (web) / `expo-audio` recorder (mobile) captures the local mic in parallel with the RTC session; on `session-ended` (or panel unmount) the buffer/`.m4a` uploads to `POST /api/walkie/messages` with `metadata:{source:"live_session", session_id}` so the clip surfaces in the timeline.
- Same async-post role gate for live join — a tech CAN live-talk on their department channel (because they CAN async-post there); a tech CANNOT live-talk on all-hands (because they CANNOT async-post there either). Locked user decision #5 ("no admin gate for live").
- `live_only` channel kind — new `POST /api/walkie/channels` accepts `{live_only:true}` (super_admin + admin only for creation). Standard channels remain `supports_live:true, live_only:false`.

**Data model additions**
- `walkie_channels.supports_live: bool` (default `True` — legacy rows get True via `WalkieChannel.from_mongo` coercion).
- `walkie_channels.live_only: bool` (default `False`).
- New `walkie_live_sessions` collection: `{id, channel_id, tenant_id, started_by_user_id, started_at, ended_at, participant_user_ids[], recording_message_id}` with indexes on `(tenant_id, channel_id, started_at desc)` + `(tenant_id, ended_at)`.
- Pydantic models `WalkieChannel` + `WalkieLiveSession` added to `backend/models.py`.

**Backend endpoints — `/api/walkie/*` additions**
- `WS /api/ws/walkie/{channel_id}?token=<jwt>` — signaling ONLY (no media relay). Client-side JWT via query param.
- `POST /api/walkie/channels` — create a `live_only` channel (super_admin + admin only).
- `GET /api/walkie/ice-servers` — Google STUN baseline + metered.ca TURN entry when the three env vars are set. Any authenticated user.

**WebSocket message-type reference**
- Client → server: `join`, `offer`, `answer`, `ice-candidate`, `speaking`, `leave`.
- Server → client: `session-state`, `peer-joined`, `peer-left`, `offer`, `answer`, `ice-candidate`, `speaking-update`, `session-ended`.
- Signaling frame set is snapshot-locked by `backend/tests/test_phase52_1d_metered_turn.py::test_signaling_*_frame_set_snapshot` — any new frame type MUST bump the snapshot deliberately.

**Room state**
- In-process `dict[channel_id, LiveRoom]` — one FastAPI worker per pod, no Redis needed. Server restart wipes the map; the 5-min `services/walkie/live_cleanup_cron.py` sweeps orphaned `ended_at IS NULL` rows whose `channel_id` no longer maps to a live in-process room.

**Auto-record extension point**
- `services/walkie/live_events.on_session_ended(session_id, reason)` fires when the last peer leaves. Phase 52.1a shipped a no-op stub; 52.1b/c wire the actual clip upload from the client side (no backend hook change).

**Roles**
- `super_admin`, `admin` — live-talk on any channel they can async-post to + create `live_only` channels.
- `manager` — live-talk on their department + directs. No `live_only` channel creation.
- `technician` — live-talk on their department + directs. No all-hands live-talk (same gate as async broadcast).
- `customer` — no walkie access (unchanged from Phase 51).

**Mesh topology + non-goals**
- Full-mesh WebRTC — every participant maintains an `RTCPeerConnection` to every OTHER participant. Practical cap **~10 peers** before we exhaust the browser's peer-connection budget and audio starts stuttering.
- Beyond ~10 peers a Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) is required — **out of scope** for the 52.1 MVP; would be a discrete Phase 52.2+ effort covering an SFU deployment (LiveKit / MediaSoup / Janus).
- Recording of `live_only` channels beyond the 24 h TTL is also **non-goal** for 52.1 — the auto-record clip enters the standard `walkie_messages` bucket and inherits the existing TTL.

**Third-party integrations**
- **metered.ca free tier TURN** — env-gated via `METERED_TURN_URLS` (comma-separated), `METERED_TURN_USERNAME`, `METERED_TURN_CREDENTIAL`. Missing any → STUN-only fallback + a startup log line. See `mobile/EXPO_GO_RUNBOOK.md#phase-521d-metered.ca-turn-wiring` for the signup + verify recipe.
- **react-native-webrtc@124.0.6** + `@config-plugins/react-native-webrtc@13.0.0` — dev-client only. iOS: `WebRTC.framework` +~9 MB. Android: `libwebrtc.so` per-ABI +~7 MB. Rebuild via `npx expo prebuild --clean` + `eas build --profile development`.

**Platform permission additions (mobile)**
- iOS `expo.ios.infoPlist.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` refreshed for live-session copy.
- iOS `expo.ios.infoPlist.UIBackgroundModes` extended with `"audio"`.
- Android `expo.android.permissions` extended with `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE` + `MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS`. Full screen-off background mic requires a native foreground-service module — **deferred** (current UX assumes phone in-hand for PTT).

**Env vars (backend)**
```
METERED_TURN_URLS=              # comma-separated TURN URLs from metered.ca
METERED_TURN_USERNAME=          # metered.ca credential username
METERED_TURN_CREDENTIAL=        # metered.ca credential secret
WALKIE_LIVE_CLEANUP_ENABLED=1   # optional; default on. 5-min stale-cleanup cron
```

**Test coverage**
- Backend `test_phase52_1a_walkie_signaling.py` — 20 tests (model round-trip, role gate on `live_only` creation, WebSocket join/relay/broadcast, stale cleanup, ICE-servers auth branches).
- Backend `test_phase52_1d_metered_turn.py` — 8 tests (STUN-only + all-set + multi-URL + partial + shape snapshot + client/server frame snapshot).
- Frontend `phase52-1b-live-panel.test.jsx` — 16 tests. `phase52-1d-walkie-live-parity.test.jsx` — 8 parity assertions.
- Mobile `phase52-1c-mobile-live-panel.test.tsx` — 11 tests. `phase52-1d-walkie-live-parity.test.ts` — 8 parity assertions.

## Phase 54 · Feb-2026 — Wholesale supplier pricebook import MVP (a → f)

Automated pricebook ingestion from five North-American pool + landscaping wholesalers via a supplier-agnostic Playwright-driven scraper framework. Delivered across six sub-phases: 54a audit + data-model skeleton, 54b Pool360 connector + Settings UI, 54c SiteOne connector + generic `test-connection` endpoint, 54d Ewing connector + `SUPPLIER_METADATA` config extraction, 54e Heritage + ePoolSupply connectors + APScheduler cron + Chromium install, 54f pricebook UI (web + mobile) supplier column + filter + Sync-all + docs.

**Feature scope**
- Five wholesalers wired: **Pool360 (PoolCorp), SiteOne, Ewing Irrigation, Heritage Pool Plus, ePoolSupply**.
- Playwright headless Chromium scraping with data-only selector config (one file per supplier) — DOM changes are patchable without code changes.
- Encrypted-at-rest credentials via Fernet (`SUPPLIER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`).
- Per-tenant, per-supplier `sync_frequency` — enum `[hourly, daily, weekly, manual]`.
- Manual "Sync now" + generic `test-connection` (~5 s, 15 s hard timeout) + super-admin "Sync all suppliers" sequential batch button.
- Daily 03:00 UTC + hourly cron (gated by `SUPPLIER_SYNC_LIVE=1`; default OFF).
- Pricebook rows carry `supplier_slug` + `supplier_id` + `external_sku` + `last_synced_at`; web + mobile pricebook show a color-coded supplier badge + filter.
- Mobile parity: read-only Settings > Suppliers screen.

**Roles**
- `super_admin` — full edit + "Sync all suppliers" button.
- `admin` — full edit + Sync now + Test connection.
- `manager` — read-only view of Settings > Suppliers (dropdown + inputs disabled).
- `technician` / `customer` — redirected out of `/settings/suppliers`.

**REST endpoints — `/api/suppliers/*`**
- `GET /suppliers` — list all supplier rows (auto-seeds 5 canonical slugs on empty read).
- `GET /suppliers/{slug}/credentials` — has_credentials flag + updated_at (no plaintext).
- `POST /suppliers/{slug}/credentials` — save encrypted credentials.
- `DELETE /suppliers/{slug}/credentials` — wipe encrypted credentials.
- `PATCH /suppliers/{slug}` — update `sync_frequency` (enum-validated) + `active` toggle.
- `POST /suppliers/{slug}/sync` — 202 + `{job_id, status: "running"}`; kicks Playwright background task.
- `POST /suppliers/{slug}/test-connection` — success + `login_failed | rate_limited | timeout | unknown` error branches.
- `GET /suppliers/{slug}/sync-jobs` — last N job rows for history table.

**Data model** (all extend `BaseDocument` per MongoDB adherence guide)
- `suppliers` — `{id, tenant_id, slug, display_name, active, sync_frequency, last_sync_at, last_sync_status, last_sync_item_count, created_at}`.
- `supplier_credentials` — Fernet-encrypted `{id, tenant_id, supplier_id, encrypted_username, encrypted_password, encrypted_api_key, encrypted_session_cookies, notes, updated_at}`.
- `supplier_sync_jobs` — `{id, tenant_id, supplier_id, started_at, finished_at, status, items_added, items_updated, items_removed, error_message}`.
- `items` (extended) — new fields `supplier_id`, `supplier_slug`, `external_sku`, `last_synced_at`, `deleted_at`, `active`.

**Env gates**
- `SUPPLIER_SYNC_LIVE=1` — enables the APScheduler daily + hourly cron to actually launch Playwright syncs. Default OFF → dry-run summaries only.
- `SUPPLIER_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` — Fernet key for credential encryption at rest.
- `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` — Playwright-native override for the Chromium cache path. Default: `~/.cache/ms-playwright`. Recommended: mount a persistent volume at this path so the ~700 MB Chromium download warms once per container fleet.

**Cron behavior**
- Two APScheduler triggers registered at startup on the existing `scheduler` singleton: `supplier_sync_hourly` (top of every hour) + `supplier_sync_daily` (03:00 UTC).
- Each tick iterates `db.suppliers.find({active: True})` and applies cadence filter + skip rules (in order):
  1. `sync_frequency == "manual"` → skip.
  2. Cadence doesn't match this tick → skip.
  3. Weekly + today isn't Sunday → skip.
  4. No `supplier_credentials` row → silently skip.
  5. Last successful sync completed <6 h ago → skip.
  6. `SUPPLIER_SYNC_LIVE != "1"` → log dry-run, return.
  7. Otherwise: `start_sync_job` + `asyncio.create_task(runner(...))`.
- Calls sync service functions directly — never self-HTTPs.
- Startup emits two log lines: `supplier.playwright: cache_path=... chromium=<ver|missing>` + `supplier.cron.registered hourly=@0min daily=@03:00UTC live=<bool>`.

**Sync frequency enum**
- `hourly` — runs from the hourly tick.
- `daily` — runs from the 03:00 UTC daily tick.
- `weekly` — runs from the 03:00 UTC daily tick, but only on Sunday.
- `manual` — never runs from cron; requires a manual "Sync now" click.

**Operator runbook**

1. **Install Chromium** (choose one — both are supported):
   - **Option A · Bake into Dockerfile**: `RUN python -m playwright install --with-deps chromium` at image build time. Image grows by ~700 MB.
   - **Option B · Persistent volume mount** (recommended): mount a persistent volume at `/root/.cache/ms-playwright` (or wherever `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` points if you override). Image stays lean; cache warms via `python -m playwright install chromium` on first container boot with empty mount. Subsequent boots reuse.
     - Docker example: `docker run -v playwright_cache:/root/.cache/ms-playwright ...`
     - Kubernetes: mount a `PersistentVolumeClaim` to `/root/.cache/ms-playwright` (or the `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` value if overridden). Cache survives pod restarts + fleet-wide replicas share it if the PVC is `ReadWriteMany`.
     - Verify after first boot: `ls /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-*` should list a `chromium-1228/` directory (version number moves with Playwright releases).
     - Startup log confirms path: `supplier.playwright: cache_path=/root/.cache/ms-playwright chromium=1228`.
2. **Save credentials** — operator navigates to `/settings/suppliers`, opens each wholesaler card, enters real username + password, clicks Save. Fernet-encrypted rows land in `supplier_credentials`.
3. **Test connection** — click "Test connection" on each card. Expect `{ok: true}` in ~5 s. Failure returns a red badge with the classified error (`login_failed | rate_limited | timeout | unknown`).
4. **Set sync frequency** — dropdown on each wired card. Default `daily`. Manual = never from cron.
5. **Enable live cron** — flip `SUPPLIER_SYNC_LIVE=1` in the backend env + `sudo supervisorctl restart backend`. The cron ticks were already firing (dry-run logging only); they now start real syncs on their next tick.
6. **Monitor** — grep `supplier.cron.` in backend logs for tick summaries. Grep `supplier.cron.launch` for individual sync starts. `POST /suppliers/{slug}/sync-jobs` returns job history.

**Legal / ToS caveat**
The Settings > Suppliers card carries a literal disclaimer under every credentials form: *"Automated syncing may be subject to your wholesaler's Terms of Service. By connecting, you acknowledge responsibility for compliance with those terms."* Operators are responsible for their own ToS compliance. The rate-limit (1 req/sec + exponential backoff up to 60 s on 429/503) is a best-effort courtesy — some wholesalers may still prohibit automated scraping regardless of politeness.

**Non-goals**
- No real supplier API integrations (no OAuth, no vendor JSON APIs). Selector-based scraping only. Future phases may replace individual connectors with vendor APIs where available; the `PlaywrightScraperBase` interface + `SUPPLIER_METADATA` map are the seams.
- No multi-currency. All prices assumed USD; the `items.cost` / `items.wholesale_price` are numeric with no currency tag.
- No historical price snapshots — the pricebook stores only the latest sync's value per SKU. Quote / invoice line items already snapshot price at issue time via the existing Phase 33 pattern.

**Test invariants at end of Phase 54**
- Vitest **1430 / 1430 pass** (from 1389 baseline → +41 across 54b/c/d/e/f).
- Mobile Jest **240 / 240 pass** (from 236 baseline → +4 in 54f parity tests).
- Backend Phase 54 curated **87 / 87 pass** (from 0 at 54a start → 87 across 54a→f including the addendum smoke tests).
- `yarn lint` exit 0.

Editable EBIT — Earnings Before Interest and Taxes — layered on top of the existing profit-report surface. Ships across backend + web + mobile with role-gated editing, immutable versioning, and PDF + CSV export. Delivered in four sub-phases (53a backend + web audit, 53b editable web UI, 53c mobile parity + seed-drift repair, 53c-fix manager read-only, 53d MVP closeout doc + contract-lock tests).

**Feature scope**
- Live compute of EBIT from cash-basis OR accrual-basis invoicing, plus expenses (COGS from line-item snapshots, OpEx + depreciation from `checks`).
- 4 editable line rows (`revenue`, `cogs`, `opex`, `depreciation`) — the `ADJUSTMENT_KEYS` — with two edit modes per row:
  - **Adjustment** (default): additive delta on top of the computed value.
  - **Override**: absolute-value replacement.
- Effective EBIT recomputes on every edit; formula `revenue − cogs − opex − depreciation`.
- **Immutable versioning**: every save inserts a new `ebit_snapshots` row with `version = max(existing) + 1`. Prior versions are never mutated. No draft/publish workflow.
- Version history modal per range on both surfaces; loading an older version puts the editor in read-only, "Fork new version" restores editability.
- **Range presets**: `monthly` (default), `quarterly`, `custom` (from / to dates) — plus server-accepted `this_month`, `last_month`, `qtd`, `ytd` for API callers.
- **Revenue basis toggle**: `cash` (default) / `accrual`.
- **PDF + CSV export**:
  - Web: `window.print()` (browser Save-as-PDF) + client-side CSV blob download.
  - Mobile: `expo-print` → `expo-sharing` (PDF) + `expo-file-system/legacy` blob → `expo-sharing` (CSV). **No new native deps** — all three were already bundled from prior phases.
- **Role gates**:
  - `EDITOR_ROLES = {super_admin, admin}` — full compute + save + PATCH.
  - `VIEWER_ROLES = {super_admin, admin, manager}` — GET only. Manager sees the panel with adjustment inputs `disabled`, flip / clear / save controls hidden, yellow `read-only` badge in the header, History + CSV + PDF exports enabled.
  - Tech + customer are 403 backend-side and rendered as the "EBIT report is admin + manager only" banner client-side.

**Endpoints — `/api/ebit/*`**

| Method | Path | Gate | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET  | `/ebit/compute?range&from&to&revenue_basis` | viewer | Live compute; no persistence. |
| GET  | `/ebit/snapshots?range_from&range_to&limit` | viewer | List saved versions (desc). |
| GET  | `/ebit/snapshots/{id}` | viewer | Fetch one saved snapshot. |
| POST | `/ebit/snapshots` | editor | Save NEW version (v1 or v+1). |
| PATCH | `/ebit/snapshots/{id}/adjustments` | editor | Merge deltas → NEW version. |
| PATCH | `/ebit/snapshots/{id}/overrides` | editor | Merge absolutes → NEW version. |

Web + mobile currently POST every save (never PATCH). PATCH endpoints remain fully tested but reserved for a future "batch quick-edit" tool.

**OpenAPI (Phase 53d)**
- `range` is a `Literal["this_month", "last_month", "qtd", "ytd", "monthly", "quarterly", "custom"]` — enum surfaces in `openapi.json`, 422 with a full-list error message on drift.
- `revenue_basis` is a `Literal["cash", "accrual"]` — same treatment.

**Data model — `ebit_snapshots`**

```
{
  id                   str (uuid)
  tenant_id            str
  range_kind           str (Literal enum, see above)
  range_from           str (YYYY-MM-DD)
  range_to             str (YYYY-MM-DD)
  revenue_basis        str (Literal enum)
  version              int (1-indexed, monotonic per (tenant, range))
  revenue              float   ← EFFECTIVE
  cogs                 float   ← EFFECTIVE
  opex                 float   ← EFFECTIVE
  depreciation         float   ← EFFECTIVE
  ebit                 float   ← revenue - cogs - opex - depreciation
  breakdown            {invoice_count, line_count, opex_payroll,
                         opex_other, opex_by_category,
                         depreciation_by_category, wages_by_role}
  computed_live        {revenue, cogs, opex, depreciation, ebit}
                                                        ← pre-edit
  line_adjustments     {revenue, cogs, opex, depreciation: float}
  line_overrides       {revenue, cogs, opex, depreciation: float | null}
  author_user_id       str
  author_display_name  str  (Phase 53d — contract-locked)
  saved_at             str (ISO-8601 UTC)
  note                 str
}
```

Indexes (idempotent):
- `(tenant_id, range_from, range_to, version desc)` → versioned history queries
- `(tenant_id, saved_at desc)` → recent-first listing

**Compute logic** — `backend/services/finance/ebit.py`

- Revenue (cash) = `Σ quote.total` on `db.quotes` where `doc_type == "invoice"` AND `payment_status == "paid"` bucketed on `paid_at` (falls back to `Σ qty × retail_price_snapshot` when the header total is empty).
- Revenue (accrual) = same query but `status ∈ {paid, partial, sent, overdue}` bucketed on `created_at`.
- COGS = `Σ qty × wholesale_price_snapshot` over the same invoice line items — matches the existing `routers/profit_report` definition so the two reports reconcile.
- Depreciation = `Σ check.amount` for non-voided `db.checks` whose effective category (LLM override in `db.expense_categories` first, else `checks.category`, lowercased) is in `{"depreciation", "amortization"}`.
- OpEx = every other non-voided check in range.
- Wages-by-role diagnostic (INFO only, not in EBIT) computed from `db.time_entries × db.users.hourly_rate`, grouped by role.

**Web + mobile surfaces**

| Surface | Route | Primary component | Sub-components |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web | `/admin/reports/profit` | `frontend/src/pages/admin/ProfitReportPage.jsx` | `frontend/src/components/admin/EbitPanel.jsx` (renders `<EbitLineRow />` × 4 + `<EbitVersionsModal />`) |
| Mobile | `/profit-report` | `mobile/app/profit-report.tsx` | `mobile/src/components/admin/EbitPanel.tsx` (same structure) |
| Route guard (web) | `AdminOrManagerForProfitReport` in `frontend/src/App.js` | targeted to this ONE `/admin/*` route | |

**Seed baseline (Phase 53c fix)**
- `seed_demo_manager()` in `backend/seed.py` — idempotent role-drift repair. On every boot, ensures `manager@aquaterra.com` resolves to `role=manager, active=True, tenant=aquaterra`. Runs unconditionally (no `SEED_DEMO_USERS` gate) so the demo baseline is self-healing.
- `test_credentials.md` — manager row corrected.

**Contract locks (Phase 53d)**
- `backend/tests/test_phase53d_ebit_contract_lock.py` — snapshots the shape of `GET /ebit/compute` + `GET /ebit/snapshots/{id}` responses (every field name + type). Any silent regression fails the test.
- `frontend/src/test/phase53d-web-mobile-ebit-parity.test.jsx` — source-inspection parity for `ADJUSTMENT_KEYS`, `EDITOR_ROLES`, `VIEWER_ROLES`, `RANGE_ENUM`, `BASIS_VALUES`, `MANAGER_READONLY_TESTIDS`, `MANAGER_HIDDEN_TESTIDS`, EBIT formula literal, POST-only client contract.
- `mobile/__tests__/phase51d-walkie-parity.test.ts` — same parity assertions on the mobile side.

**Non-goals (explicitly deferred)**
- Draft / publish workflow — every save is immediately visible; there's no "in-progress" state. Version history + Fork is the substitute.
- External accounting sync (QuickBooks / Xero / Sage). The compute reads directly from CRM tables; no round-trip.
- Budget-vs-actual variance analysis. EBIT is a single-figure computation; comparing against a budget line is a separate report.
- Consolidated multi-entity EBIT (parent-tenant roll-up). Every snapshot is scoped to a single `tenant_id`.
- Automatic period lock (fiscal year close). Anyone with editor role can save a new version to any range at any time.

**Test coverage**
- Backend pytest: `test_phase53a_ebit_backend.py` (25 tests — role gates, compute correctness for cash + accrual, save + version, adjustments, overrides + null-fallback, tenant isolation, manager viewer/editor split) + `test_phase53c_seed_manager.py` (1) + `test_phase53d_ebit_contract_lock.py` (6).
- Frontend vitest: `ebit-panel.test.jsx` (14) + `ebit-panel-manager-readonly.test.jsx` (7) + `phase53d-web-mobile-ebit-parity.test.jsx` (11).
- Mobile jest: `phase53c-mobile-ebit-panel.test.tsx` (13) + `phase51d-walkie-parity.test.ts` (34, of which 15 are EBIT parity).
