## Feb-2026 · Door-hanger email — Part A + Part B (Auto-send on completion)

**Part A (copy/design)** — already shipped in prior turn. This entry
documents Part B (Auto-send + shared builder refactor).

### Files changed
- `backend/routers/workstream_service_log.py` — extracted the body
  builder + Resend dispatcher into shared helpers
  (`_build_door_hanger_email`, `_compose_and_send_door_hanger`),
  added `maybe_auto_send_door_hanger(jid, tenant_id)` +
  `schedule_auto_send_door_hanger` fire-and-forget wrapper. Manual
  endpoint now uses the shared dispatcher with `actor="manual"`.
- `backend/routers/jobs.py` — hooked `PUT /api/jobs/{jid}` at the
  `pending→completed` transition (line ~1076) to schedule the
  fire-and-forget auto-send.
- `backend/routers/service_reports.py` — hooked
  `POST /api/jobs/{jid}/service-report/submit` (line ~452) to
  schedule the fire-and-forget auto-send when the submit flow flips
  the job status to `completed`. Captures `_prev_status` BEFORE the
  update.
- `backend/routers/mobile_sync.py` — hooked `_handle_job_close`
  (mobile offline sync replay) with the same transition guard so
  mobile-driven completions also fire once.
- `backend/tests/test_door_hanger_auto_send.py` — **NEW.** 8 tests
  covering all 7 contract points.

### Contract
* Trigger: fires on `previous_status != "completed"` →
  `new_status == "completed"` from THREE write paths:
  `PUT /api/jobs/{jid}`, `POST /api/jobs/{jid}/service-report/submit`,
  and `mobile_sync._handle_job_close`.
* Idempotency: unique `marketing_event_ledger` row keyed
  `(tenant_id, customer_id, event_key="door_hanger_auto:{job_id}")`.
  Insert-first so concurrent completions cannot double-send;
  `DuplicateKeyError` = skip silently.
* Opt-out fields honoured: `customer.unsubscribed`,
  `customer.do_not_contact`, and `subscribers.status ==
  "unsubscribed"` (Marketing M1 mirror). Manual endpoint bypasses
  all three (admin override).
* Skip paths still stamp the ledger `sent` so we do NOT retry-loop;
  a `marketing_deliveries` row with `provider_status="skipped"` is
  logged with the reason.
* Non-blocking: dispatched via `asyncio.create_task(...)` — the
  completion API returns 2xx before Resend is called.
* Never raises: outer helper catches all exceptions, logs, returns
  `{"status": "error", ...}`.

### Tests
`backend/tests/test_door_hanger_auto_send.py` — 8/8 passing:
1. First completion → one ledger + one delivery + one Resend call.
2. Repeat completion → no extra rows / no extra Resend calls.
3. `could_not_service` → no ledger, no delivery, no Resend.
4. No customer email → ledger sent, delivery `skipped`, no Resend.
5. `customer.unsubscribed=True` → skip with reason
   `customer_unsubscribed`.
6. `customer.do_not_contact=True` → skip with reason
   `customer_do_not_contact`.
7. Manual endpoint AFTER auto-send → not blocked by the auto ledger
   key; produces its own manual delivery row.
8. Internal crash inside builder → helper never raises; returns
   `{"status": "error"|...}`.

Full `test_door_hanger_auto_send.py` + `test_door_hanger_email_body.py`
suite → **12/12 passing** in 1.76s.

## Feb-2026 · Homeworks Import Center · P0 Unstick + Inactive lifecycle mapping

### Root cause (stuck QUEUED · Running…)
`services/homeworks_mcp/import_dispatcher.py` had NO watchdog / recovery
mechanism.  A doc claimed to `running` by a pod that then died (crash,
OOM, deploy roll) stayed `running` forever — no scheduled tick would
re-pick it (the atomic `queued → running` flip filters `status:"queued"`
by design).  Compounded by `_dry_run_cache` being in-memory (a pod
restart lost the dry-run window, so re-submitting also failed with
`dry_run_required_within_15_minutes_before_run`).

### Fixes shipped
1. **Watchdog** in `dispatcher_tick()`.  Sweeps `{queued, running}`
   docs whose `updated_at` is older than `WATCHDOG_STALE_MINUTES=15`
   with `counters.customers_scanned == 0`, transitions them to
   `failed_stale`, appends an `error_log` row with the reason.
2. **Reset-stuck admin endpoint** —
   `POST /api/integrations/homeworks/imports/dispatcher/reset-stuck?kind={optional}`
   (super_admin only).  Flips any stuck `{queued, running}` doc back
   to `queued`, clears the `dispatcher_pid` / `dispatcher_claimed_at`
   lock fields, kicks a dispatcher tick immediately if the 5s cooldown
   window is clear.  Preserves `counters` + `resume_cursor` so a mid-
   flight run resumes.
3. **Structured transition logs** — every `queued → running`,
   `running → <terminal>`, and `<stuck> → failed_stale` now emits
   one `[dispatcher] transition …` line so ops can reconstruct a
   run's lifecycle from `grep '[dispatcher]'`.
4. **Inactive lifecycle mapping** — Homeworks `INACTIVE` /
   `WRITTEN_OFF` now stamps our canonical `customer.is_active = False`
   (the exact field `routers/customers.py` line 261 filters on).
   Raw label preserved as `customer.source_status` so churn analysis
   can distinguish the two.  Idempotent update path (`_build_backfill_update`)
   only fills missing fields — never overwrites non-null local
   edits, and never flips `is_active` if a local edit set it back to
   True.
5. **Refined counters** — `customers_created` / `customers_updated` /
   `customers_skipped` / `customers_marked_inactive` (plus legacy
   `customers_imported` = created + updated for BC).  FE
   progress line updated to show all four.

### Files changed
- `backend/services/homeworks_mcp/import_dispatcher.py` — watchdog +
  transition logging + `_try_start_run` log line.
- `backend/routers/integrations_homeworks_dispatcher.py` — new
  `POST /reset-stuck` endpoint.
- `backend/services/homeworks_mcp/inactive_customers_importer.py` —
  `_map_customer` stamps `is_active=False` + `source_status`;
  `_customer_exists` returns the doc for the update path; new

## Feb-2026 · Chemistry required-readings gate (5 core fields)

### Business rule
A pool job cannot transition to ``completed`` unless all five core
chemistry readings are present + parse as a real finite float:

1. Free Cl (free_chlorine)
2. Total Cl (total_chlorine)
3. Alkalinity
4. pH
5. CYA (cyanuric_acid)

Optionals (water temp, calcium hardness, anything else on the
checklist) can still submit blank.  Missing = ``null`` / ``""`` /
whitespace / unparseable string.  ``0`` and negative floats are
VALID readings.

### Single source of truth
**`backend/services/chemistry_gate.py`** —
`assert_core_readings_present(source)` raises a structured 422:

```json
{
  "detail": "chemistry_core_readings_missing",
  "missing_fields": ["free_cl", "ph", "cya"],
  "message": "Cannot close job — required chemistry readings missing"
}
```

Accepts both the ``service_reports.chemical_readings`` list-of-dicts
shape AND the legacy ``jobs.chemical_readings`` flat dict.  Aliases
(``free_cl`` / ``cya`` / ``alk`` / ``total_alkalinity`` / etc.) fold
onto canonical keys.

### Backend enforcement — all 3 paths call the same helper
1. `POST /api/jobs/{jid}/service-report/submit` (routers/service_reports.py)
2. `PUT  /api/jobs/{jid}` — only when payload flips `status → "completed"` (routers/jobs.py)
3. `mobile_sync._handle_job_close` — the offline-replay path (routers/mobile_sync.py)

**Could-Not-Service and any other non-``completed`` status change
is NOT gated.**  Landscape jobs are exempt (`is_pool_job()` check).

Mobile offline replay returns the 422 inline so the client's SQLite
queue holds the row until the tech fills the readings — no silent
drop.

### Frontend mirrors
* **Web (React)** — `frontend/src/utils/chemistryGate.js` +
  `frontend/src/pages/tech/ServiceReport.jsx`:
  * Submit button disabled while any core is missing.
  * Native `title` tooltip lists the exact missing labels
    ("Missing: Free Cl, pH, CYA").
  * On 422 from a stale UI → dismissible inline warning banner
    (does NOT lose the tech's other entered data).
* **Mobile (Expo)** — `mobile/utils/chemistryGate.ts` +
  `mobile/app/(app)/service-report/[id].tsx`:
  * Submit button disabled + amber "Missing: …" hint line above it.
  * `Alert` fallback if the client mirror lets a stale submit
    through and the backend 422s.
  * Offline queue row is NOT dequeued on 422 — tech can re-open,
    fill readings, and re-sync (SQLite read cache from Offline
    Phase 1 untouched).

### Files changed
* `backend/services/chemistry_gate.py` — **NEW**, single source of truth.
* `backend/routers/service_reports.py` — gate on submit.
* `backend/routers/jobs.py` — gate on PUT transition to completed.
* `backend/routers/mobile_sync.py` — gate on `_handle_job_close`.
* `backend/tests/test_chemistry_required_readings_gate.py` — **NEW**, 11 cases.
* `frontend/src/utils/chemistryGate.js` — **NEW**, web mirror.
* `frontend/src/pages/tech/ServiceReport.jsx` — button disable + tooltip + inline banner.
* `mobile/utils/chemistryGate.ts` — **NEW**, mobile mirror.
* `mobile/app/(app)/service-report/[id].tsx` — button disable + hint + Alert fallback.

## Feb-2026 · Water-test bands hotfix (customer-facing views)

### What shipped
Raw ppm/pH values are gone from customer-facing surfaces. Instead:

| Reading    | Below Average | Average | Above Average | Elevated |
| ---------- | ------------- | ------- | ------------- | -------- |
| Free Cl    | < 1           | 1 – 5   | 5 – 10        | ≥ 10     |
| Total Cl   | < 1           | 1 – 5   | 5 – 10        | ≥ 10     |
| pH         | < 7.2         | 7.2–7.6 | 7.6–8.2       | ≥ 8.2    |
| Alkalinity | < 80          | 80–120  | 120–140       | ≥ 140    |
| CYA        | < 30          | 30–80   | 80–150        | ≥ 150    |

**Boundary rule (user-approved):** lower INCLUSIVE, upper EXCLUSIVE.
So Free Cl == 1.0 → Average, Free Cl == 5.0 → Above Average, Free Cl == 10 → Elevated.

⚠️ **Free Cl / Total Cl "Above Average" (5–10) and "Elevated" (≥ 10)
thresholds are main-agent defaults surfaced for user confirmation.**
pH, Alkalinity, CYA thresholds are user-approved verbatim.

1. Door hanger email — Water Test section in `_build_door_hanger_email`.
2. Portal service-report detail page (`/portal/service-reports/:id`) —

### Where exact numbers STAY

- Anywhere behind admin/super_admin auth

### Optional readings (water_temp, calcium_hardness)
- Filled → render exact value + unit
- Blank → row OMITTED entirely (no "N/A" placeholder)

**Data model**
* `tos_documents` — versioned per (tenant, service_type∈{pool,landscaping}); status draft|published; at most one current published per (tenant, service_type) enforced by write-time supersede.
* `tos_acceptances` — audit; version + service_type + source.
* `customer.tos_status = {pool: {version, accepted_at} | null, landscaping: {...} | null}` + `tutorial_completed_at`.

**Endpoints**
* Admin CRUD + `POST /tos-documents/{id}/publish` (supersede + notify).
* Customer `GET /portal/onboarding-state` returns `{needs_tutorial, pending_tos: [pool-first, then landscaping]}`.
* Customer `POST /portal/tos/accept` writes audit + updates customer map.

**Sanitizer** — `bleach.clean` allow-list; strip script/style/iframe/on-handlers; auto-inject `rel="noopener noreferrer"` + `target="_blank"` on external `<a>`.

**Editor auth** — admin + super_admin only.

**Sub-phases (hard-stop points A-D)**
* 2A · Backend foundation + seed migration (existing content → pool v1) + 20+ pytest cases.
* 2B · Admin UI at `/settings/legal/terms-of-service`; TipTap editor; two service-type tabs; draft/publish + confirm dialog; version history sidebar.
* 2C · Customer portal `OnboardingGate` — Tutorial → pool ToS → landscaping ToS in order; partial-acceptance persistence; scroll-to-bottom + I Agree; dangerouslySetInnerHTML with client-side DOMPurify defence-in-depth.
* 2D · Publish → notification email blast to customers with matching active `service_type`; door-hanger skip rules honored; `marketing_event_ledger` key `tos_update:{document_id}` for idempotency; non-blocking; magic-link deep-link back to portal.

**Cross-cutting locked rules**
* Legal audit trail — never hard-delete published/superseded rows.
* Cross-service isolation — publishing pool ToS never notifies landscaping-only customers.
* Both-service customer — gets both emails, both modals (pool first).
* Version bump re-prompts ONLY the bumped ToS.

**Position in queue** — slot #2, after #4 (chemical cost hide) lands.

**Do not start** — needs a full fresh session's context runway.
Hard-stop at any of 2A/2B/2C/2D boundaries.

**Locked decisions carried in** — 1a (service classification from `service_type` on customer / active jobs / active recurring subscriptions), 2 yes-to-all (sequenced modals, partial-acceptance persistence, per-service version-bump re-prompt), 4a (TipTap → bleach server-sanitized), 5b (Draft/Publish manual button), 6b (admin AND super_admin edit).

**Data model**
* `tos_documents` — one row per `(tenant_id, service_type, version)`. Fields: `id`, `tenant_id`, `service_type ∈ {"pool","landscaping"}`, `version` (monotonic per (tenant, service_type)), `status ∈ {"draft","published","superseded"}`, `title`, `content_html` (server-sanitized), `content_json` (TipTap doc), `effective_date`, `created_at/by`, `published_at/by`, `superseded_at`.
* `tos_acceptances` — one row per `(tenant_id, customer_id, document_id)` with a unique compound index. Fields: `id`, `tenant_id`, `customer_id`, `document_id`, `service_type`, `document_version`, `accepted_at`, `ip`, `ua`.
* Embedded fast-lookup on `customers.tos_status.{pool|landscaping}` = `{document_id, version, accepted_at}` so `compute_pending_tos_for_customer` avoids a joined query.

**Backend files**
* `backend/services/tos_service.py` (new) — sanitizer (bleach allow-list with `<a>` hardening + `javascript:` block), service-type classifier (customer.service_type + customer.service_types + active jobs + active subs; completed jobs ignored), `current_published_docs`, `compute_pending_tos_for_customer` (canonical pool→landscaping order), `record_customer_acceptance` (atomic acceptance row + embedded-map update), `publish_document` (draft → published with atomic supersede of prior published row), `next_version_for`, `seed_pool_tos_from_legacy` (idempotent boot migration wrapping `TOS_MARKDOWN` in `<pre>`), `ensure_indexes`.
* `backend/routers/tos_multi.py` (new) — admin CRUD (`GET/POST /admin/tos-documents`, `GET/PUT/POST /admin/tos-documents/{id}[/publish]`) + customer endpoints (`GET /customer-portal/onboarding-state`, `POST /customer-portal/tos/{document_id}/accept`). All admin writes go through the sanitizer. `PUT` rejects edits on non-draft rows with 409 (legal audit invariant). Publish is idempotent. Customer-portal handlers reject non-`role=customer` with 403.
* `backend/server.py` — registered `tos_multi` router; boot hook adds `ensure_indexes` + `seed_pool_tos_from_legacy` per tenant (runs after existing `run_tos_backfill`). Seed logged as `[slice-2a] multi-tos seed: N tenant(s) seeded`.
* `backend/requirements.txt` — added `bleach==6.4.0` (+ `webencodings==0.6.1` transitive).

Coverage:
- Sanitizer (5): strips `<script>/<style>/<iframe>`, preserves TipTap marks + lists + `<blockquote>` + `<hr>`, hardens external `<a>` with `rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"`, blocks `javascript:`, empty/null returns `""`.

- Customer flow (8): pending includes only pool for pool-only customer, only landscaping for landscape-only customer, canonical order pool→landscaping for both-services customer, acceptance stamps row + embedded-map update, post-acceptance pending shrinks to zero, version bump re-triggers pending for THAT service_type only (partial-acceptance persistence), unknown-document acceptance rejects, unpublished-document acceptance rejects.

## Feb-2026 · Queue Item #2 · Sub-phase 2C — Customer Portal OnboardingGate · ✅ SHIPPED

**New component** `frontend/src/components/legal/OnboardingGate.jsx`
* Fetches `GET /customer-portal/onboarding-state` on mount, renders one blocking modal per entry in `pending_tos` (server-sorted pool → landscaping), advances via `POST /customer-portal/tos/{document_id}/accept`, unmounts when the array empties. On error the server-returned `pending_tos` snapshot swaps in — no client-side state divergence.
* **Role-gated** — no-op unless `user.role === "customer"`. Admin / super_admin / technician / manager flow through untouched.
* **Scroll-gate** — "I Agree" button disabled until the modal body reaches `scrollTop + clientHeight >= scrollHeight - 8`. Auto-enabled when the doc is short enough to fit without scrolling (30ms post-mount check).
* **Blocking UI, escape-hatch preserved** — modal is full-viewport at `z-[85]` with backdrop; NO dismiss X, NO Reject button. But **children remain mounted** (rendered alongside the modal, not replaced), so the shell header + Sign Out button stay reachable at `z-50` above the backdrop-blocking overlay.
* **DOMPurify NOT added** — dep isn't in `package.json`, scope guard forbids adding. Server-side `services/tos_service.sanitize_html` (bleach allow-list, `javascript:` blocked, external `<a>` auto-hardened) is the sole HTML gate. `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` used on the sanitized `content_html`.
* **409 `document_not_published`** on accept → inline error banner ("This version is no longer active. Reloading…") + auto-refresh 400ms later so the freshly-published superseding version loads.

**Legacy `TosGate.jsx` decision — REPLACE (via sibling), don't adapt**
* Reasoning: legacy `TosGate` is single-doc (`/legal/tos`), non-loopable, gates on `user.must_accept_tos`, and posts to `/users/me/accept-tos`. Adapting would require rewriting 90% of the file AND blurring which system is authoritative for which audience. Cleaner to co-mount: legacy `TosGate` keeps admin single-doc flow untouched (self-gates on `must_accept_tos`, unrelated to `role`); new `OnboardingGate` handles customer per-service flow (self-gates on `role === "customer"`, orthogonal predicate). Predicates don't overlap.

**Tutorial component — deferred with gap surfaced**
* `PortalWalkthrough.jsx` exists in the customer portal but its completion is tracked client-side only. The 2A DTO exposes `tutorial_completed` (server-side) but **does not expose** a `POST /customer-portal/tutorial/complete` endpoint. The 2C scope guard freezes the 2A backend, so this iteration stubs `needs_tutorial=false` (`_STUB_NEEDS_TUTORIAL = false`) with a jsdoc pointer explaining what needs to land to enable the tutorial leg.
* **Gap surfaced for a future 2A follow-up**: add `POST /customer-portal/tutorial/complete` that sets `customers.tutorial_completed_at` + returns fresh `onboarding-state`. One-line flip in `OnboardingGate` to wire it up.

**Mount location** `frontend/src/layouts/AppLayout.jsx`
* Wrapped the `<Outlet />` inside a single `<OnboardingGate>...</OnboardingGate>` block right after `<Breadcrumbs />`. Legacy `<TosGate />` still mounted above at line 341 — the two gates coexist by role predicate.

**Tests** `frontend/src/test/portal-onboarding-gate.test.jsx` (new) — **7/7 vitest pass**:
1. Non-customer role (admin / super_admin / technician / manager) → children render immediately, no API calls.
2. Fully onboarded customer → children render, no modal, no accept POST.
3. Pool + landscaping pending → pool renders first (asserts `data-service-type="pool"` + title); accept POSTs `/customer-portal/tos/d-pool/accept`; then landscaping renders; second accept unmounts the modal.
4. Only landscaping pending → landscaping modal renders (skip pool).
5. `I Agree` disabled until scroll bottom (jsdom trick: force `scrollHeight > clientHeight` on all elements, simulate scroll event, assert button toggles).
6. 409 `document_not_published` → inline error banner + reload; modal stays open.
7. Sign Out in header remains in the DOM while modal open.

**Regression** — Frontend **45/45 pass** across 7 suites (2C + 2B + job-edit-window + concierge-avatar + portal-bands + portal-invite-relocation + phase27-portal-sections). Backend **106/106 pass** — 2A untouched.

## Feb-2026 · Queue Item #2 · Sub-phase 2D — Publish Notification Blast · ✅ SHIPPED

**New portal auto-login scope** (`services/portal_magic_links.py`)
* `mint_portal_home_token(customer_id, tenant_id, *, ttl_hours=48)` — `sub="portal_home"`, 48h TTL. Reuses HS256 + `JWT_SECRET` — no new signing scheme.
* `verify_portal_home_token(token)` — rejects wrong-scope with `401 token_wrong_scope`, expired/tampered with `401 token_invalid_or_expired`, malformed with `401 token_malformed`.
* `build_portal_home_url(base_url, customer_id, tenant_id)` — stamps `/api/portal/auto-login?t={token}`.
* `_classify_and_verify` in `routers/portal_auto_login.py` — 4th probe entry `("portal_home", verify_portal_home_token)`. On match → `default_target = "/portal/home"`, `resource_id = None`. All 4 scopes mutually exclusive (each verifier rejects any other scope with `token_wrong_scope`).

**Blast worker** (`backend/routers/tos_multi.py`)
* `publish_tos_document` — fires `asyncio.create_task(_run_publish_blast(...))` after the DB transition. Task-schedule failure caught and logged; publish endpoint still returns 200.
* `_run_publish_blast` — upsert-first-then-dispatch matching `door_hanger_auto` / `elevated_followup_shown`:
  1. Insert `marketing_event_ledger` row keyed `tos_update:{doc_id}` FIRST. `DuplicateKeyError` → blast skipped entirely (retry / race safe).
  2. Query recipients via new `services.tos_service.customers_with_active_service` (reuses `classify_customer_services` so blast recipients ≡ customers who'll see the pending ToS on next login).
  3. Per recipient → `_blast_one_customer` writes one `marketing_deliveries` row with status `sent` / `skipped` / `failed`. Skip reasons: `no_email`, `unsubscribed`, `do_not_contact`. Resend adapter failure → `status=failed`, `provider_status=failed`, error captured in `skip_reason` (truncated to 200 chars).
* Every exception at the task boundary caught + logged — publish endpoint never depends on Resend availability.

**Email template** — card-based inline-styles-only layout matching Slice 5 door-hanger visual system:
* Subject: `Updated Terms of Service — {tenant.name}`
* Hero header card (brand color background) with `UPDATED TERMS` eyebrow + company name
* Body card with `Hi {first_name},` greeting + 2-sentence warm non-alarming copy ("We've updated our Terms of Service for {pool|landscaping} customers. Please review and accept the updated terms at your next portal visit — this email is for your records; the portal will prompt you when you sign in.")
* `Review Updated Terms` CTA button pointing at `build_portal_home_url(...)` — auto-login → `/portal/home` → OnboardingGate (2C) picks up the new pending ToS
* Footer: `We appreciate your business` + tenant name + phone

**New index** (`services/tos_service.ensure_indexes`) — `marketing_event_ledger` compound unique on `(tenant_id, event_key)` name `uniq_tenant_event_key`. Idempotent — no-op if another module already owns it.

**Tests** — `backend/tests/test_tos_multi_2d_publish_blast.py` (new). **8/8 pass**:
1. Pool publish → per-recipient `marketing_deliveries` row for active-pool customers only.
2. Landscaping-only customer NOT emailed on pool publish (cross-service isolation).
3. Skip rules — `no_email` / `unsubscribed` / `do_not_contact` each logged with reason, no send.
4. Second `_run_publish_blast` for same doc → ledger key blocks (only 1 send, only 1 ledger row).
5. Resend adapter raises → `marketing_deliveries.status="failed"` + `provider_status="failed"` + error captured, worker never re-raises.
6. Cross-scope replay: `portal_home` token rejected by all 3 other verifiers AND `portal_home` verifier rejects all 3 other tokens (401 `token_wrong_scope`).
7. Auto-login route accepts `portal_home` token → 200 interstitial with `/portal/home` redirect + `localStorage.setItem('token', …)` seeded.
8. Sequential pool + landscaping publish → dual-service customer gets both emails; 2 distinct ledger rows.

### Homeworks `Customer.discount` GraphQL bug · ✅ SHIPPED

Root cause: Homeworks removed the scalar `discount` field from the
`Customer` type in their live schema; our local `schema.graphql`
snapshot at line 705 was stale. Both cohort page queries selected the
field → `GRAPHQL_VALIDATION_FAILED` on every dry-run and real run.
Delta Sync's `both_cohorts_failed_dry_run` was the aggregated fatal
from the shared query failure.

**Fix:** dropped the `discount` selection from `CUSTOMER_PAGE_QUERY`
(inactive) and `ACTIVE_CUSTOMER_PAGE_QUERY` (active) in
`services/homeworks_mcp/queries.py`. No mapper change — grep
confirmed no downstream code read `customer["discount"]`. Estimate-level
`discountPercent` / `discountAmount` untouched. Top-of-module drift
note documents the removal + points to the original error signature.

**Queue-button gating** already correct pre-fix (`HomeworksImportCenter.jsx:213`
guards on `!!fatal`); the 1,317 / 1,496 candidate counts users saw
were legit — they come from the id-only `COUNT_PAGE_QUERY` at
`inactive_customers_importer.py:126` which succeeded before the sample
fetch failed. No frontend changes required.

Tests: `backend/tests/test_homeworks_discount_field_drop.py` · 6/6.

## Phase P32 · Feb-2026 — Muted-tab exclusivity + custom-reason auto-persist

### Root cause of the reported bug
- P27 mute path stamps BOTH `is_active=False` AND `is_muted=True` on the customer doc.
- The P28 list-endpoint Inactive filter was `is_active=false` **only** (no `is_muted != true` guard), so every muted row also satisfied Inactive → they appeared under Inactive with a MUTED badge AND under the (correct) Muted tab. Counts inherited the same bug because they reuse the same query.

### Files changed
- `backend/routers/customers.py`
  - `list_customers` — Active + Inactive branches now AND with an explicit `is_muted != true` guard.
  - `mute_customer` — after successful mute with a reason, invokes new `_p32_auto_persist_reason` helper (wrapped in try/except so any failure is swallowed and never blocks the mute).
- `frontend/src/components/customers/MuteControl.jsx` — clears local `reasons` cache on successful mute so next open re-fetches the auto-persisted row.
- `mobile/src/components/customers/MuteControlSheet.tsx` — same cache clear on success.
- `backend/tests/test_customer_muted_exclusivity_p32.py` — new (8 tests).
- `frontend/src/test/phase32-mute-reason-cache-invalidation.test.jsx` — new (2 tests).

### Auto-persist contract (`_p32_auto_persist_reason`)
- Case-insensitive dedup via `label_norm` across active + archived rows for the tenant.
- Missing → insert `is_active=true`, next `sort_order+10`, `auto_created=true`, audit event `muted_reason_auto_created`.
- Matches active → no-op.
- Matches archived → NO reactivation; customer.muted_reason snapshot still stored on the customer as free-text (historical snapshots stay immutable).
- Empty / whitespace reason → skip entirely.
- Wrapped in try/except at the call-site so a Mongo failure never unwinds the mute.

### Results
- **New backend tests: 8/8 green** (`test_customer_muted_exclusivity_p32.py`) covering Active/Inactive/Muted/All exclusivity, novel auto-persist, active-reason no-dup, archived-reason no-reactivate, and no-reason skip path.
- **New frontend tests: 2/2 green** (`phase32-mute-reason-cache-invalidation.test.jsx`) covering cache clear on mute + cache untouched on unmute.
- **P25/P26/P27/P28/P29/P29b/P30/P32 combined backend sweep: 52/52 green.**
- **Mobile Jest MuteControlSheet: 6/6 green.**
- `/api/openapi.json` still 200. Live curl confirms Muted count endpoint reachable and returns integer.

### Guardrails honored
- `bbeck169/Pool-Landscaping.git` ignored.
- `test_config_public_returns_show_demo_logins` untouched.
- Reused `not_deleted_filter()` helper.
- Auto-persist wrapped in try/except (isolation from mute path).
- Archived reasons NOT auto-reactivated.
- `customer.muted_reason` remains free-text — no FK coupling.

## Phase P34 · Feb-2026 — Automation quiet-hours window

### Investigation summary (before code)
- **~25 direct callers** of `send_sms()` / `send_email()` across the codebase — Option B (patch each call-site) rejected. Went with Option A hybrid: gate at two adapter chokepoints (`services/comms_sms_adapter.py::send_sms` + `services/comms_email_adapter.py::send_email`), inheriting coverage for all 25 callers.
- **APScheduler `AsyncIOScheduler`** already runs 38 jobs in `server.py`. Added 1 new interval job (5 min) matching the existing style.

### Files added
- `backend/services/quiet_hours.py` — `is_within_send_window`, `next_send_window_open`, `defer_send`, `claim_pending_batch`. Handles same-day + overnight windows.
- `backend/services/quiet_hours_context.py` — `contextvars`-backed `bypass_gate()` for the release worker to skip the gate on re-dispatch.
- `backend/services/quiet_hours_release.py` — `run_release_tick()` used by both scheduler + on-demand endpoint.
- `backend/routers/quiet_hours_settings.py` — `GET/PATCH /api/settings/quiet-hours` + `POST /api/internal/quiet-hours/release`.
- `backend/migrations/task_p34_quiet_hours_defaults.py` — one-shot backfill (dry-run default).
- `backend/tests/test_quiet_hours_p34.py` — **16/16 green**.
- `frontend/src/pages/settings/QuietHoursPage.jsx` — settings UI.
- `frontend/src/test/phase34-quiet-hours-settings.test.jsx` — **5/5 green**.

### Files touched
- `backend/services/comms_sms_adapter.py` + `.../comms_email_adapter.py` — insert quiet-hours gate at the top of each send; returns `status="deferred"` with the row id when out-of-window.
- `backend/server.py` — router registration + APScheduler wiring.
- `frontend/src/App.js` — route wired behind `AdminOrManagerForMutedReasons` gate (identical role set; reused rather than duplicated).
- `frontend/src/nav/adminNav.js` — nav entry under "Schedule & Dispatch" next to Muted Reasons.

### Deferred send row shape (`outbound_deferred`)
```
{ id, tenant_id, channel: "sms"|"email", payload: {...adapter args...},
  scheduled_for: ISO-UTC (next window-open), created_at, created_by,
  released_at, status: "pending"|"releasing"|"sent"|"failed",
  provider_id?, release_result? }
```
Enough context to re-dispatch identically after the window opens (no ephemeral in-process state).

### Backfill migration output (preview DB)
```
committed: True · total_tenants: 24 · backfilled: 24 · missing_timezone_warnings: 0
```
All 24 preview tenants now carry `quiet_hours_enabled=false` + defaults; existing sends continue unchanged.

### Judgment calls (transparent)
1. **Did NOT gate the `resend.Emails.send` SDK-level monkey-patch** (`services/comms/sdk_intercept.py`). That layer has no tenant context. The two canonical adapters (`send_sms`/`send_email`) carry the tenant_id and are the ONLY authorized send paths in the codebase — every marketing / drip / reminder / lead-notification path routes through them. Any bare `resend.Emails.send` call is a legacy pattern outside our automation surface and is not gated.
2. **Release worker uses `contextvars`-based bypass** rather than a marker in the payload/headers dict. Rationale: `send_sms` has no headers surface, so headers-based marker would only work for email. `contextvars` is task-scoped and safe under concurrency.
3. **Windows with `start == end`** are hard-rejected (400 on PATCH) — otherwise it means "always closed" and would silently start dropping mail forever.
4. **Fail-open on gate errors** — if `is_within_send_window` throws for any reason, the adapter logs a warning and sends anyway. Prevents a bug in the gate from becoming an outage.

### Results
- **P34 backend tests: 16/16 green** — pure time-logic + settings RBAC + release worker + idempotency + backfill idempotency.
- **P34 frontend tests: 5/5 green.**
- **P15b + P25 → P34 combined backend sweep: 90/90 green.**
- Scheduler boots cleanly: `scheduler: p34 quiet-hours release tick registered (every 5 min)`.
- `/api/openapi.json` still 200.
- Pre-existing `test_config_public_returns_show_demo_logins` untouched.

### Files added
- `backend/routers/gps_auto_start.py` — GET/PATCH `/api/settings/gps-auto-start`; GET/POST `/api/tech-gps-consent(/me)`; helpers `is_gps_auto_start_enabled`, `get_arrival_radius_m`, `has_active_consent`, `rate_limit_check` (60s per (user, job), matches Phase 20A.3 idiom).
- `backend/migrations/task_p37_geocode_backfill.py` — customers + jobs + properties, dry-run default, `--tenant` + `--limit` flags, per-row failure isolation.
- `backend/tests/test_gps_auto_start_p37a.py` — **14/14 green** (openapi, settings RBAC + validation, consent grant/revoke roundtrip, /arrive gate order, throttling, success + audit log, auto-stop on service-report submit, auto-stop regression on PUT status→completed).

### Files touched
- `backend/models.py` — `JobArriveIn.accuracy` optional field for audit-log breadcrumbs.
- `backend/services/google_maps/geocoding.py`
  - `geocode_and_persist_customer` — now writes canonical `latitude/longitude` alongside legacy `service_lat/lng` (dual-field for back-compat).
  - New `geocode_and_persist_job` — checks own address then falls back to inheriting from linked customer's already-geocoded coords (no double-charge).
  - New `geocode_and_persist_property` — from structured `address` doc.
- `backend/routers/jobs.py::job_arrive`
  - Reuses existing endpoint (does NOT create a new one).
  - Added 4 gates in short-circuit order: `feature_disabled` → `consent_required` → `throttled` → `out_of_radius`. Each 200s with a `reason` string so mobile can keep polling.
  - Distance via `services.geofence_engine.haversine_m` (meters, existing helper).
  - Persists to both `site_lat/lng` (legacy) and `latitude/longitude` (canonical) fields.
  - Audit-logs `job_timer_auto_start` with `{arrival_lat/lng, site_lat/lng, distance_m, radius_m, accuracy_m}`.
- `backend/routers/service_reports.py::submit` — **fills the auto-stop gap**: on submit, if timer running, stamps `timer_stopped_at`, `timer_duration_seconds`, `timer_stop_method="service_report_submitted"` + audit-logs `job_timer_auto_stop`.
- `backend/server.py` — registers the new router.

### Migration output (preview DB)
```
committed: True
  customers   scanned=  5  geocoded=  0  skipped=  5   (all 5 have empty address fields)
  jobs        scanned= 18  geocoded= 18  skipped=  0
  properties  scanned=147  geocoded=124  skipped= 23   (empty/malformed addresses)
```
Migration is idempotent + resumable via `--limit`.

### Judgment calls (transparent)
1. **Reused existing `/jobs/{jid}/arrive`** rather than creating a new `/job-timer/auto-start` endpoint. The existing endpoint already did 80% of the work (timer stamping, method labeling, coord persistence, RBAC). Wrapping the four P37a gates around it kept the diff minimal and preserved all existing mobile callers (Phase 20A.3 auto-clock-in flow).
2. **Rate-limit is per-worker, in-memory** (not Redis-backed). Matches the exact pattern used by `/workforce/auto-clock-in`. Acceptable given the 60s window and the single-worker preview deployment; if we scale horizontally we can promote to Redis in a follow-up.
3. **Dual-field persistence** — geocoder now writes BOTH `service_lat/lng` (legacy) AND `latitude/longitude` (canonical) on customers. Same for jobs (`site_lat/lng` + `latitude/longitude`). This is a transitional shim; a future P37c-ish tidy phase can consolidate to `latitude/longitude` only once all callers are migrated. Zero downtime, zero break risk.
4. **NOT geocoding synchronously on customer POST/PUT** — the migration + Phase 20A.3-era hooks already do the persistence pattern. Adding another synchronous geocode-on-write would double-execute for the customer path. Decision: leave hot request paths untouched; the migration covers backfill; the existing on-write helpers cover the update path (already there in `geocode_and_persist_customer`).

### Results
- **P37a backend tests: 14/14 green.**
- **Combined regression sweep (P15b + P25→P37a): 115 passed / 1 skipped** — no regressions.
- `/api/openapi.json` still 200.
- Pre-existing `test_config_public_returns_show_demo_logins` untouched per guardrails.

## Feb-2026 · Multi-Body Service Reports — Phase 1 (backend) — SHIPPED

**Problem**: A single service visit can involve multiple bodies of water on the same property (Pool + Spa + Water Feature + Fountain). The legacy schema only carried one flat set of `chemical_readings` / `chemicals_added` / `photos` per report — techs had no way to log distinct chemistry / chemicals / media / notes per body, and Customer History / Chemical Cost surfaces couldn't split rollups by body.

### Design decisions (approved)
- **Type picker (fixed)**: `pool | spa | water_feature | fountain | other`.
- **Trimmed chemistry allow-lists per type**:
  | Body type | Readings allowed | Required | Chemicals allowed |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | pool | FC, TC, pH, TA, CYA, Calcium, Salt, TDS, Phosphates | 5 canonical (FC/TC/pH/TA/CYA) | all 9 |
  | spa | FC, pH, TA, Calcium | — soft-warn only | 7 (no CYA-stab, no salt bag, no PO4-remover) |
  | water_feature | FC, pH | — | 5 (LC, MA, Clarifier, Enzymes, PO4-remover) |
  | fountain | FC, pH | — | 5 |
  | other | any (free-form) | — | any |
- Only `pool` bodies gate submit; the other four are soft-warn.
- `water_bodies[0]` seeded with a single default body on bootstrap; migration back-fills legacy reports (24 docs on preview).

### Schema
```
service_reports.water_bodies = [
  { id, type, label, sequence,
    readings: [{ key, name, unit, value, ts, not_tested? }],
    chemicals_used: [{ product_slug, name, quantity, unit, ... }],
    media: [{ url, kind, tags?, ... }],
    notes: str }
]
```
Legacy top-level `chemical_readings` / `chemicals_added` / `notes` remain populated (mirror) so auto-invoice, `snapshot_chemical_usage`, doorhanger renderer, mobile sync — every legacy consumer — keep working without a body-aware rewrite.

### Files touched

## Feb-2026 · Option 2 — Chemical-cost report rewrite — SHIPPED

**Symptom (from tester Bug #3)**: Multi-body invoice `6e64b146-…` returned zero chlorine_tabs across `/api/reports/chemical-costs` even after submit stamped 2 valid `chemical_usage_events`. Root cause: report aggregated from invoice line items (which the submit-path auto-invoice never emits per-chemical) and looked for `wholesale_cost_snapshot` (typo — canonical field elsewhere is `wholesale_price_snapshot`).

**Fix (Option 2 — pivot to `chemical_usage_events` as source of truth)**:
- `snapshot_chemical_usage` now accepts a `water_bodies` param and iterates each body's `chemicals_used`, stamping every event with `water_body_id / water_body_type / water_body_label`. Legacy `chemicals_added` callers still work — get `water_body_id=None`.
- Service-report submit passes `water_bodies` to the snapshot when the report has them; falls back to the flat `chemicals_added` mirror otherwise.
- `/api/reports/chemical-costs` rewritten to aggregate from `chemical_usage_events` filtered by `occurred_at`; joins `db.quotes` on `job_id` for the "paid work only" gate (bypassable via `include_unpaid=true` for admin audit). Adds `by_water_body` bucket splitting rollups per body with a synthetic `legacy` bucket for pre-migration events.
- Idempotent boot migration `chemical_usage_events_water_body_v1` back-fills legacy events. Best-effort retro-links to a body when the parent report has exactly one body OR a unique body carries a chemical whose slug matches. Ambiguous cases stay `water_body_id=None`.
- Admin endpoint `POST /api/admin/migrations/chemical-usage-events-water-body?force=` for on-demand re-runs.
- Fixed the `wholesale_cost_snapshot` typo transparently — the report no longer reads invoice snapshots at all.

**Empirical proof (invoice 6e64b146-2c00-47c4-a25a-f3b1a6f29976 paid)**:
```
by_water_body:
  {water_body_id: 1771fa81-…, body_type: pool, body_label: Main Pool,
    total_qty: 1.0, total_wholesale_cost: 0.75, chemical_count: 1, job_count: 1}
  {water_body_id: fa3d9684-…, body_type: spa,  body_label: Backyard Spa,
    total_qty: 0.5, total_wholesale_cost: 0.38, chemical_count: 1, job_count: 1}
by_chemical[0]: chlorine_tabs qty=1.5 total=$1.13
totals: {qty:1.5, cost:$1.13, jobs:1}
```
BOTH bodies visible; totals reconcile.

**Files touched**:
- **New**: `services/migrations/chemical_usage_events_water_body.py` (sentinel `chemical_usage_events_water_body_v1`), `tests/test_chemical_usage_events_water_body.py` (7 tests).
- **Modified**: `routers/chemical_products.py` (`snapshot_chemical_usage` iterates `water_bodies`); `routers/chemical_cost_report.py` (rewritten — aggregates from events + adds `by_water_body`); `routers/service_reports.py` (submit passes `water_bodies` to snapshot); `routers/admin_migrations.py` (adds CUE backfill endpoint); `server.py` (boot migration hook); `tests/test_chemical_cost_report.py` (rewritten to seed events + paid invoices).

- `test_service_report_multi_body.py` — 17/17 passing (backward-compat preserved).

## Feb-2026 · Invoice inline edit + Pricebook writeback — SHIPPED

**Blocker resolved:** User reported the New Invoice page rejected saves with `Unknown or archived category: 'Common'` AND locked the unit_price field on product-typed pricebook items. Both fixed.

**Parts:**

**A · Unlock inline pricing:**
- `_enforce_item_type_price_lock` (`quotes.py`) softened — no more 400 on product-price drift. Now just stamps `overridden_price=True` on the line for downstream margin reports. Strict-mode opt-in via `STRICT_PRODUCT_PRICE_LOCK=1` env for anyone who wants the pre-Feb-2026 behaviour back.
- Frontend: `QuoteInvoiceNew.jsx` unit-price input is a plain editable `<input type="number">` — no `readOnly`, no `disabled`, no lock icon. When the price diverges from the pricebook default an amber-bordered field + `"custom price — pricebook shows $X.XX"` hint appears.
- `InvoiceEditModal.jsx` (edit surface) was already unlocked; only added writeback + inline error surfaces.

**B · Inline category picker + robust error handling:**
- New: `QuoteInvoiceNew.jsx` now mounts `<CategoryPicker>` on every line (required, source=income). Populated from `/api/income-categories`.
- `CategoryPicker.jsx` extended: `+ Add category` option at bottom of the dropdown opens an inline "create category" form wired to `POST /api/income-categories/resolve-or-create`. Newly-created rows are pushed into the module-scope cache and auto-selected on the offending line.
- `CategoryPicker.jsx` extended: `invalidReason="archived_category"` prop renders a red-border + inline warning chip so the caller can force the operator to pick a new category before saving.
- `income_categories.py` error shape widened: `detail.error_code`, `detail.line_index`, `detail.attempted_category` added alongside the legacy `error` / `field` keys — frontend consumes these to highlight the offending row.
- Frontend save handlers on BOTH surfaces (`QuoteInvoiceNew` + `InvoiceEditModal`) parse the structured error and surface it INLINE on the offending row (`data-testid="qf-line-{N}-row-error"` and `data-testid="invoice-edit-line-{N}-row-error"`). Save button stays enabled — operator fixes inline + retries.

**C · Pricebook writeback (per-line):**
- New: `services/pricebook/writeback.py` — `process_pricebook_writebacks()` fans out AFTER a successful invoice save transaction. Rules: (i) tenant-scoped only, (ii) FK-match wins if the line has a pricebook FK, else case-insensitive name match on the tenant's items, else create a new row with `source="invoice_writeback"`, (iii) never blocks the invoice save.
- Every writeback audited to a new `db.pricebook_writeback_events` collection with `{tenant_id, invoice_id, line_item_id, pricebook_item_id, action, before, after, actor_user_id, actor_email, actor_role, source, created_at}`.
- Wired into `quotes.py` (`POST /quotes`, `PUT /quotes/{qid}`) and `invoice_edit.py` (`PATCH /quotes/{qid}` alias). Post-save fan-out only.
- Frontend: per-line checkbox with dynamic label — "Also save this to the pricebook" (line has FK) vs "Also add this to the pricebook" (free-text line becomes new pricebook item). Unchecked by default. Ships on BOTH surfaces.

**D · Data integrity + tenant isolation:**
- `writeback.py._process_pricebook_writebacks` scopes every read/write to the caller's `tenant_id`. Cross-tenant FKs fall through to the name-match branch (which stays within the caller's tenant) — verified by `test_invoice_writeback_tenant_isolation.py`.

Validates MIME (`image/png` / `svg+xml` / `webp` / `jpeg`), enforces 2 MB max (413 with `error_code=file_too_large`), rejects unsupported MIME with 415 (`error_code=unsupported_media_type`), persists to Emergent Object Storage under `poolcrm/<tenant_id>/branding/logo/<uuid>.<ext>`, stamps `tenant.logo_url` + `logo_object_path` + `logo_content_type` + `logo_size_bytes` + `logo_updated_at` + `logo_updated_by_user_id`. ## Phase I3 — Post-Deploy Health-Checker Admin Endpoint (Feb 2026) — SHIPPED

### What shipped
- **New endpoint**: `GET /api/admin/health-check/comprehensive` (super_admin only). Never 5xxes — every failure encoded in the payload.
- **10 checks, each timed independently**:
  1. `boot_state` — F4 integrity scan complete + dangling_refs / enforce-mode
  2. `mongo_ping` — 0.5s timeout ceiling
  3. `required_migrations` — `["perf_customers_v1"]`
  4. `optional_migrations` — pending count of non-required `migration_status` rows
  5. `hotpath_smoke` — direct DB probe of `customers` + `jobs` + internal `_k8s_health_ready()` call (NO HTTP round-trip)
  6. `comms_gate` — `services.comms_hardening.dispatch_guard` module + callable check
  7. `rc_sms_from_number` — `RingCentralSMSAdapter._resolve_from(tenant_id)`, response never leaks the number
  8. `scheduler` — APScheduler running-state + job count, respects `ENABLE_SCHEDULER=false` split-deployment posture
  9. `env_sanity` — `EMERGENT_LLM_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `RC_SMS_DEFAULT_FROM` (missing=fail, empty=warn)
  10. `feature_gates` — informational snapshot with recovery-mode note when `INTEGRITY_CHECK_ENFORCE=false`

- **Verdict**: `GO` / `GO_WITH_WARNINGS` / `NO_GO`. `fail` → NO_GO, `warn` → GO_WITH_WARNINGS.
- **UI**: `HealthCheckCard.jsx` on `/admin/migrations` between DataIntegrityTile and DriftAlertsCard. Click → modal with color-coded verdict banner + per-check rows + recommendations + Copy JSON.

### Files
- `/app/backend/routers/admin_health_check.py` (507 LOC, new)
- `/app/backend/tests/test_admin_health_check_comprehensive.py` (420 LOC, new — 9 tests)
- `/app/frontend/src/components/admin/HealthCheckCard.jsx` (346 LOC, new)
- `/app/frontend/src/test/admin-health-check-modal.test.jsx` (217 LOC, new — 12 tests)
- `/app/backend/server.py` (+5 LOC — router registration)
- `/app/backend/tests/_f7_loop_fixture.py` (+2 entries — `routers.admin_health_check` + `utils`)
- `/app/frontend/src/pages/admin/AdminMigrationsPage.jsx` (+2 LOC — import + render)

### Tests
- Backend: 9 tests. Covers happy path, required-migration-missing NO_GO, dangling_refs+enforce=true NO_GO, dangling_refs+enforce=false GO_WITH_WARNINGS (recovery mode), RBAC (admin/tech/unauth all rejected), always-200 contract, feature-gate informational status.
- Frontend: 12 tests. Covers trigger button, modal open, all 3 verdict colors, per-check rows, recommendations rendering + hiding, Copy JSON clipboard call, Copy disabled on error, summary counts, close.
- Loop fixture surprise: `utils.py` imports `db` at module scope from `config`. Prior fixture didn't rebind it, so any JWT-authenticated ASGI test via `httpx.ASGITransport` failed with "attached to a different loop". Adding `"utils"` to `_REBOUND_MODULES` fixed it — safe for every JWT-gated test going forward.

### Live curl proof (preview `aquaterra` tenant)
```
=== VERDICT: NO_GO
=== SUMMARY: {'checks_total': 10, 'ok': 7, 'warn': 1, 'fail': 2}
=== RECOMMENDATIONS:
 - Boot integrity scan failed — check backend startup logs and run the F2 data-repair dry-run before declaring GO.
 - Missing required env vars: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY. Deploy is misconfigured — set them and redeploy.
 - SOSHIE_MODERATION_ENABLED is unset (defaults to enabled) — set explicitly for clarity.
 - SOSHIE_REGEX_PREFILTER_ENABLED is unset (defaults to enabled) — set explicitly for clarity.
=== NON-OK CHECKS:
 [FAIL] boot_state: dangling_refs_total=14, integrity_check_enforce=true
 [WARN] hotpath_smoke: health_ready http_status=503 (downstream of the boot_state failure)
 [FAIL] env_sanity: missing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY (test env not seeded in preview)
```

### Screenshots
- `/tmp/phase_i3_health_check_modal.png` — modal rendered against the real preview verdict, red NO_GO banner, all 10 check rows visible, Copy JSON + Done in footer.

### Surprises about internal state accessibility
- `_F4_BOOT_INTEGRITY_STATE` is a module-level dict in `server.py` — accessible via lazy `import server` from the check function; safe against import-cycle because we defer until the check runs.
- `_k8s_health_ready` is defined at module scope in `server.py` and can be called directly from a router handler (no HTTP round-trip). Returns a bare dict when healthy or a `JSONResponse` when not — the check normalizes both shapes.
- `_REQUIRED_MIGRATIONS` was defined **inside** `_k8s_health_ready` (function-local) rather than at module scope; duplicating the list into `routers/admin_health_check.py` was cheaper than refactoring the readiness handler.
- `RingCentralSMSAdapter` re-instantiates cleanly per-call — safe to construct one for the check without polluting a singleton.

### Non-goals honored
- No PII leaked (RC number surfaced as `resolved: true, length: 12`, not the actual number).
- k8s probe endpoints untouched.
- No mobile changes.
- No auto-polling — manual on-demand only.

## Phase I4 — Soshie Brand-Ingest Async Job Pattern (Feb 2026) — SHIPPED

### Problem
Human reported the `/soshie` "Re-ingest brand memory" flow timing out on prod with the 30s frontend fetch cap. Sync ingest crawls 1-13 pages + parses HTML; a cold site on a slow origin easily blows the budget.

### What shipped
- **New endpoints** (all `require_admin`, tenant-scoped):
  - `POST /api/soshie/brand-brain/ingest` → **202 Accepted** with job row + `Location: /api/soshie/brand-brain/ingest/<id>` header. Returns in <500ms.
  - `GET /api/soshie/brand-brain/ingest/{job_id}` → job row (404 on missing/cross-tenant).
  - `GET /api/soshie/brand-brain/ingest/latest` → most recent tenant job, `{job: null}` when empty. Drives the resume banner.
- **Legacy shim**: `POST /api/soshie/ingest-website` still returns 200 with a `{async_job: true, job_id, poll_url, pages_fetched: 0, ...}` envelope — historical shape preserved for mobile + bookmarks.
- **Worker**: `asyncio.create_task`-spawned. Wraps under `asyncio.wait_for(_do_ingest, timeout=300)` (5-min ceiling). Every exception path writes `status="failed", error=<200 char>` to the job row — never crashes the process.
- **Path cap**: `MAX_TOTAL_PATHS=5` (home + 4 extras). Router returns 400 with `detail: too_many_paths` when caller submits more; worker re-enforces defensively.
- **Stale-job sweep**: `cleanup_stale_ingest_jobs` registered as APScheduler `interval, minutes=5, id="soshie_ingest_stale_sweep"`. Marks any `running` job older than 15 minutes as `failed, error="timeout_stale"` — belt-and-suspenders for pod-died-mid-job.
- **Progress signal**: worker updates `progress.paths_crawled`, `progress.paths_total`, `progress.current_step` at each phase (`queued` → `fetching_home` → `crawling_and_parsing` → `merging_brand_brain` → `succeeded`).

### Frontend
- `BrandBrainTab.jsx` modal now polls `GET /ingest/latest` every 5s while open. Success → toast + auto-close. Failure → modal stays open with a **Retry** button and the truncated error message.
- **Resume banner** at the top of the tab on mount: `Ingest in progress — <step> · N/M pages` with an "Open modal" affordance.
- Modal cancel button relabels to **"Close (keeps running)"** when a job is in-flight — the operator can walk away and check back.

### Files
- `/app/backend/services/soshie/brand_ingest_jobs.py` (365 LOC, new)
- `/app/backend/routers/soshie_brand_ingest.py` (120 LOC, new)
- `/app/backend/tests/test_soshie_brand_ingest_async.py` (474 LOC, new — 12 tests)
- `/app/frontend/src/test/soshie-brand-ingest-async.test.jsx` (248 LOC, new — 7 tests)
- `/app/backend/server.py` — router register + scheduler cron entry (+16 LOC)
- `/app/backend/routers/soshie_publishing.py` — legacy endpoint shimmed to async (rewrite of `ingest_website_endpoint`)
- `/app/backend/tests/_f7_loop_fixture.py` — add `routers.soshie_brand_ingest`, `routers.tenants`, `services.soshie.brand_ingest`, `services.soshie.brand_ingest_jobs` to `_REBOUND_MODULES`
- `/app/frontend/src/pages/soshie/BrandBrainTab.jsx` — full rewrite of IngestModal + resume banner

### Tests
- Backend: **12 tests passing** — 202 shape, GET status returns progress, worker error encoding, `wait_for` timeout → `error="timeout"`, stale-sweep marks failed with `error="timeout_stale"` (untouched fresh jobs), `>5 paths → 400`, RBAC tech/unauth 403, `/latest` returns most-recent tenant-scoped job (cross-tenant leak guard), `/latest` returns `{job: null}` on empty tenant, worker writes brand_brain fields on success, legacy endpoint shim.
- Frontend: **7 tests passing** — resume banner on mount when running, no banner on terminal, POST fires + progress shown, poll success → toast + close, poll fail → modal stays open + Retry, `extra_paths` textarea splits/trims correctly, regression guard against re-introducing the legacy sync endpoint.

### Live curl proof (preview)
```
=== POST /api/soshie/brand-brain/ingest ===
HTTP/2 202 
location: /api/soshie/brand-brain/ingest/88143b5a-0a61-40a3-ace3-07eac2040e71
{"id":"88143b5a-...","status":"queued","started_at":"...","progress":{"paths_crawled":0,"paths_total":2,"current_step":"queued"},"result_summary":null}

=== poll cycle (1s intervals) ===
poll #1 · status=succeeded · progress={paths_crawled: 2, paths_total: 2, current_step: succeeded} · error=None
```
POST returned in ~500ms, real crawl of `https://example.com` + `/about` completed in under 1s (small target), status transitioned `queued → running → succeeded` cleanly.

### Screenshot
- `/tmp/phase_i4_ingest_progress.png` — modal shows `RUNNING` pill, "Ingest in progress — this can take 1-3 minutes." message, `Step: crawling_and_parsing · Pages 0/2` counter, `Close (keeps running)` + `Ingesting…` footer buttons.

### Surprises
- The current sync `ingest_website` has **no LLM call** — it's pure BeautifulSoup + regex distillation. The brief mentioned a 30s LLM ceiling; I surfaced `LLM_TIMEOUT_S=30` as a module constant for future LLM steps but the current timeout risk is HTTP crawl latency, not model inference. Encoded as an overall 5-min `asyncio.wait_for` on the worker.
- The legacy endpoint uses `get_current_user` (any auth), but the new endpoints use `require_admin`. Kept the legacy gate as-is to preserve behavior; new admin-only endpoints are the primary surface going forward.
- `_f7_loop_fixture.py` needed **two additional module rebinds** (`routers.tenants`, `services.soshie.brand_ingest`) because both hold module-scope `db` references that JWT-authenticated ASGI tests hit. Same class of bug I3 tripped over with `utils`.
- The legacy `POST /soshie/ingest-website` shim writes an idempotent cache entry via `store_response`; if a client retries with the same `X-Idempotency-Key` they get the SAME `job_id`, not a new one. Cheap deploy-safety for mobile.

## Phase I5 · Wave A — Payment Method Tiles (Admin, Feb 2026) — SHIPPED

### Wave scope
Ship the foundation (backend delete gate) + admin mount. Wave B (customer portal Billing Method tab mount) queued for next session.

### Audit findings
Existing endpoints already covered LIST + ADD (SetupIntent) + plain DELETE:
- `GET  /api/payments/stripe/payment-methods/{customer_id}` — mirror list, `payment_methods` array with fields `{id, provider_payment_method_id, type, brand, last4, exp_month, exp_year, bank_name, account_holder_type, is_default}`
- `POST /api/payments/stripe/setup-intent` — Add flow
- `POST /api/payments/stripe/attach` — attach after SetupIntent
- `DELETE /api/payments/stripe/payment-methods/{pm_id}` — plain detach (kept as-is for B-series callers)

Added: **`POST /api/payments/stripe/payment-methods/{pm_id}/delete-typed`** with body `{typed_last4: str}` — reloads the mirror row and re-validates the typed keyword against the stored `last4` before calling Stripe. Returns 400 `typed_last4_mismatch` on wrong keyword, 404 on unknown/cross-tenant PM, 200 on success with `{ok, last4, type, brand}`.

### Frontend
- **`PaymentMethodTiles.jsx`** (487 LOC, new) — shared component, `variant: "admin" | "portal"`. Renders:
  - Credit/Debit Cards subsection: green on-file tile (`colors.landscape[50/300/700]`) with masked number `•••• •••• •••• {last4}`, expiry `MM / YYYY`, padlock glyphs on each field. Edit + Delete buttons per tile.
  - Bank Accounts subsection: same green treatment with account/bank/type fields.
  - Empty state: saturated dark-red (`colors.error` + `colors.onError`) container with bold copy `"No Credit/Debit Card Information Found for This Customer"` / `"No Bank Account Information Found for This Customer"` and a white Add CTA below.
  - Delete → `TypedConfirmModal` (H2 pattern) keyed on `pending.last4`; POST body carries `typed_last4`; server re-validates.
  - Add → inline expand of existing `StripeAddCardForm` / `StripeAddBankForm`.
  - Edit → also opens the inline Add form of the same type with an info toast: "Card/bank details are immutable — add a new one, then delete the old." Stripe PMs are immutable post-attach so this is the correct semantic.
- **Mount**: `CustomerDetail.jsx` Overview tab, between `cd-customer-name-secondary` heading and `CustomerContactsPanel` (per screenshot mockup).

### Tests
- **Backend**: **11 tests** — correct keyword deletes + calls Stripe once, wrong keyword rejects without calling Stripe, whitespace-trimmed but exact-match, unknown PM 404, empty stored last4 short-circuits to 400 (guards legacy rows), tech 403, customer-owns-PM 200, customer-not-owner 403, unauth 401/403, cross-tenant 404, ACH bank flow returns `type=us_bank_account`.
- **Frontend**: **11 tests** — loading state + card + ACH tiles, empty states, Add-card CTA opens inline form + refetches, delete modal armed by typing last4 + POST body contract, delete failure keeps modal open + error toast, Edit opens Add form + info toast, Bank delete uses "Bank account ending in…" copy, no fetch when customerId is null, admin-placement source-body contract (name → tile → contacts ordering + `variant="admin"` + exactly ONE mount).

### B-series regression
`test_stripe_ach_admin_attach.py`, `test_stripe_customer_sync.py`, `test_stripe_health_probe.py`: 28 passing after this change. `test_payment_methods_delete.py` + `test_admin_health_check_comprehensive.py`: 20 passing.

### Live curl proof (preview)

```
→ HTTP 400 · {"detail":"typed_last4_mismatch"}    ✅ gate correctly rejects

Body: {"typed_last4":"2589"}
→ HTTP 502 (Stripe API rejects the fake PM id)    ✅ gate passed validation

                                                     is the correct downstream
```

### Screenshot
- `/tmp/phase_i5_admin_tiles.png` — captured against a real seeded VISA · 2589 · exp 12/2030 mirror row on `/customers/<id>`. Shows green on-file card tile with padlock-locked masked fields, Edit + Delete buttons, and the dark-red empty state for Bank Accounts with `Add Bank Account` CTA. Placement matches mockup: between customer name heading and Contact card.

### Surprises
1. **Stripe PMs are immutable**: the mockup shows Edit buttons but Stripe's PaymentMethod API doesn't allow editing card details post-attach. Wired Edit to reopen the inline Add form + surface an info toast so operators aren't confused. No new endpoint needed.
2. **`AdminCardCapturePanel` already existed** with a working add flow; I reused its underlying `StripeAddCardForm` / `StripeAddBankForm` primitives rather than the panel itself so the tiles can render side-by-side with them elsewhere on the page without duplicated Stripe iframes.
3. **Loop fixture needed two more rebinds** (`routers.stripe_router`, `services.payments.stripe_charge`) for JWT-authenticated ASGI tests — same pattern I3/I4 hit. Added to `_REBOUND_MODULES`.
4. **B1 mirror shape**: `payment_methods` collection carries a `type` discriminator (`"card"` | `"us_bank_account"`) — the tiles filter on that field. ACH rows have `bank_name` + `account_holder_type`; card rows have `brand` + `exp_month/year`. Both share `last4` which is what the typed-delete keyword validates against.

## Phase I7 · Wave A — Communication Timeline (Admin, Feb 2026) — SHIPPED

### Endpoint spec
`GET /api/customers/{customer_id}/communication-timeline?limit=50&before=<iso>&types=sms,email`

- RBAC: admin/manager/super_admin see any tenant customer; role=customer sees only their own (`user.customer_id == customer_id`); tech 403; unauth 401/403.
- Query params: `limit` (1-200, default 50) · `before` (iso timestamp cursor) · `types` (csv: `sms,email` — filter both server-side).
- Response:
  ```json
  {
    "customer_id": "...",
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "...", "type": "sms" | "email",
        "occurred_at": "iso",
        "actor_label": "admin@aquaterra.com" | "System / Automation",
        "actor_kind": "user" | "system",
        "actor_user_id": "u_...",        // admin only
        "direction": "outbound",
        "channel_id": "...",
        "subject": "..." | null,
        "body_preview": "first 500 chars",
        "recipient": "phone or email",
        "delivery_status": "sent" | "delivered" | "queued" | "failed" | "reserved",
        "delivery_error": "..." | null   // admin only
      }
    ],
    "has_more": bool,
    "next_before": "iso" | null
  }
  ```
- Portal filtering: when `user.role == "customer"`, server strips `actor_user_id` + `delivery_error` from every item before returning. The wire response never carries admin-only fields for portal callers — a frontend regression cannot leak them.

### Data sources (audit surprises)
- **`notification_dispatch_log`** — the primary source. Per-message row for every SMS + email dispatch flowing through the F7 idempotent notifier + F5 marketing sequences. Fields consumed: `channel` (`sms` | `email`), `recipient_id` (== customer_id when the sender wired it), `resolved_address` (fallback match against customer's `email`/`phone`), `subject`, `status`, `sent_at` / `reserved_at`, `error`, `metadata.body`, `metadata.actor_email`, `metadata.actor_user_id`.
- **`audit_events`** — supplementary, one event type included: `portal_invite_bulk`. Merged in via `payload.customer_ids` array (or `payload.customer_id` fallback) matching the requested customer. Emitted as a synthesized email row with subject `"Portal invite"` and a bullet-style body preview.
- **`email_delivery_log`** — **INTENTIONALLY EXCLUDED**. Preview audit revealed this is a **weekly digest batch log** (`week_start`, `week_end`, `total_completed`, `total_skipped`, `recipients` list) — not a per-message log. A per-customer view would require denormalizing the recipients list, and the same underlying per-email rows already land on `notification_dispatch_log`. Excluding it prevents double-counting and keeps the query surface honest. Documented at the top of `routers/communication_timeline.py`.
- **`audit_events` event_types in preview**: only 3 distinct types exist (`data_integrity_digest`, `portal_invite_bulk`, `test_tenant_purge`). Of those, only `portal_invite_bulk` carries per-customer semantics via `payload.customer_ids`; the other two are tenant-wide operational events with no customer linkage. Constant `_AUDIT_EVENT_TYPES = ("portal_invite_bulk",)` is extensible when new event types with customer_id land.

### Files
- `/app/backend/routers/communication_timeline.py` (261 LOC, new)
- `/app/backend/tests/test_communication_timeline.py` (394 LOC, new — 10 tests)
- `/app/backend/server.py` (+7 LOC — router registration + wire comment)
- `/app/backend/tests/_f7_loop_fixture.py` (+1 rebind entry — `routers.communication_timeline`)
- `/app/frontend/src/components/customers/CommunicationTimeline.jsx` (289 LOC, new)
- `/app/frontend/src/pages/customers/CustomerDetail.jsx` (+13 LOC — Clock icon import, tab entry, tab body, component import)
- `/app/frontend/src/test/communication-timeline.test.jsx` (244 LOC, new — 13 tests)

### Tests
- **Backend (10 passing)**: merge + sort desc, `types=sms` filter, `before` cursor pagination (no page overlap), customer-own-record + portal field stripping, admin sees `actor_user_id` + `delivery_error`, customer-can't-view-other 403, tech 403, empty customer returns empty list, cross-tenant isolation, `portal_invite_bulk` audit event surfaces with correct actor.
- **Frontend (13 passing)**: loading skeleton, empty state, red SMS pill + green Email pill copy, bolded actor next to "by", admin variant status pill + error line, portal variant hides both admin-only fields (defense-in-depth on top of server stripping), load-more fires with `next_before` cursor + appends items, skips fetch when `customerId` is null, error banner, admin placement (import present, tab between Notes and Credits, single mount inside `tab === "timeline"` with `variant="admin"` + `customerId={id}`).

## Phase K14 — Bulk-Charge Silent-Failure Fix + Audit Deltas (Feb 2026) — SHIPPED

Redirected from the original K14 dispatch (which would have re-built the bulk-charge feature) after audit revealed Phase 14b already ships this capability. Scope was narrowed to: (1) surface the "silent no-op" via toasts, and (2) add two K13-adjacent audit stamps.

### Root cause of the "silent no-op" on Prod
1. Dry-run bypasses Stripe entirely (`_init_api_key()` is only called on real charges), so eligibility-mode `POST /api/invoices/bulk-charge-card-on-file?dry_run=true` returns 200 regardless of Stripe config — the modal renders eligibility rows.
2. If **every** customer's PM is missing / mode-mismatched, dry-run marks all rows `no_card_on_file` → `would_charge=0` → the modal disables the "Confirm charge" button. Admin sees a table full of skips with **no toast**, no explanatory banner — feels like the button broke.
3. Even if a real charge fires and `_UnconfiguredStripeError` bubbles from a missing `STRIPE_MODE=live` + `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_LIVE` on the Prod pod, the router's try/except records the row as `failed` (200 OK). The existing frontend fires `toast.error` on `summary.failed>0` — but the mount-time dry-run failure path and the confirm-fetch throw path both **only rendered an inline error block, never a toast**. If the modal was covered or dismissed, admins saw nothing.

### Fix delivered
**Frontend — `frontend/src/components/invoices/BulkChargeModal.jsx`** (three surfaces):
- Mount-time `dry_run` catch → `toast.error("Bulk charge check failed: <msg>")`.
- `confirm()` catch → `toast.error("Bulk charge failed: <msg>")`.
- Success path: added `toast.warning` for the "all skipped, nothing charged" and "eligibility ok but no cards to charge" cases so admins don't miss a functional-but-empty run.

**Backend — `backend/services/payments/stripe_charge.py`**:
- `charge_card_on_file` and `_persist_charge` now accept `via_impersonation: bool = False` + `acting_admin_id: Optional[str] = None`. Every `stripe_charges` row (the "payments" ledger) carries the K13 stamp on both success and failure paths. Defaults preserve every existing call-site.

**Backend — `backend/routers/invoices_bulk_charge.py`**:
- Forwards `user["is_impersonated"]` / `user["impersonator_id"]` (populated by `utils.get_current_user` from the JWT `act` claim) into the service call.
- Inserts a `db.audit_events` row (`event_type="invoice_auto_charged"`) after every successful charge. Payload carries `invoice_id`, `customer_id`, `amount_cents`, `currency`, `payment_intent_id`, `bulk_run_id`, `payment_method_id`, `invoice_number`; top-level fields include `via_impersonation` + `acting_admin_id` so the timeline renderer can badge impersonated actions.

**Backend — `backend/routers/communication_timeline.py`**:
- Adds `invoice_auto_charged` to `_AUDIT_EVENT_TYPES` + a dedicated `_audit_to_item` branch that renders it as `type="payment"` with amount, PI tail (`pi_…abc123`), and `(via impersonation)` suffix when the row is impersonated.
- Extends the audit-include filter to also fire when the client asks `types=payment`.

### Tests
- **New file `backend/tests/test_k14_bulk_charge_audit.py`** — 3 tests:
  1. `test_k14_non_impersonated_charge_stamps_row_and_emits_audit` — direct admin bulk-charge writes `via_impersonation=False`, `acting_admin_id=None` on both the payments ledger row and the `audit_events` row.
  2. `test_k14_impersonated_charge_stamps_row_and_emits_audit` — impersonated request (JWT `act` claim → `is_impersonated=True` + `impersonator_id`) writes `via_impersonation=True` + correct `acting_admin_id` on both rows AND asserts the kwargs flowed from router→service.
  3. `test_k14_audit_event_surfaces_on_communication_timeline` — end-to-end HTTP: the audit row appears as a `type=payment` item on `GET /api/customers/{cid}/communication-timeline` with correct amount + impersonation flag.
- **Full regression:** 28/28 pass across `test_bulk_charge_phase14b.py` (15), `test_communication_timeline.py` (10), `test_k14_bulk_charge_audit.py` (3).

### Curl proof of the failure surface (preview)
Confirmed on preview: sending an unpaid invoice with a stub PM through `POST /api/invoices/bulk-charge-card-on-file?dry_run=false` returns `summary.failed=1` (row-level `error_code`, `error_message`) — the frontend's `toast.error(<summary>)` now fires. The pre-existing `stripe_charges_pi_unique` index collision on `null` PI ids is orthogonal (see `known_issues.md`) and out of K14 scope.

### RCA for Prod
The silent behavior on Prod is a **frontend-observability gap** compounded by **missing Prod Stripe env vars**. Env vars (`STRIPE_MODE=live`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_LIVE`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET_LIVE`, `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY_LIVE`) must be set on the Prod pod for a real charge to succeed. Even before that env fix, admins now see a toast on every failure path so a live regression won't be silent again.

### Next Action Items (deferred)
- Set the four Prod Stripe env vars on the live pod (identified during K1 RCA; needed for portal payments too).
- Optional: add a permanent inline banner inside `BulkChargeModal` when `_UnconfiguredStripeError` is detected in the failure detail, guiding ops to set the env var directly (P2).
- Fix the pre-existing `stripe_charges_pi_unique` index collision on null PI ids so retried failures don't cross-collide (P1 — separate ticket).

## Phase K41b · Feb-2026 — Bulk Resolve picker on Data Integrity modal (SHIPPED)

### Backend — `backend/routers/dashboard_drilldown.py`
- **New endpoint** `POST /api/dashboard/data-integrity/resolve-bulk` (Admin + super only, 403 otherwise).
- Body: `{ items: [{ref_class, job_id, action, target_id?}], bulk_batch_id?: uuid }` — server mints a UUID when the client omits it.
- **Batch cap** `_BULK_CAP = 100`; requests exceeding it return `400 batch_cap_exceeded_max_100`. Empty items → `400 items_required`.
- Extracted `_apply_resolve_item(...)` helper shared by single-row + bulk endpoints — zero behavioural change to `POST /api/dashboard/data-integrity/resolve`.
- **Per-row audit** — every emitted `dashboard_drilldown_edit` event carries the shared `bulk_batch_id` in the extras.
- **K6 hook preserved** — `_emit_k6_completion_audit` still fires per row for completed jobs.
- **Idempotency** — in-memory `_bulk_idempotency_cache` (60s TTL) replays the identical response for the same `bulk_batch_id`; no re-mutation, no duplicate audits.
- **Never rolls back** — per-row failures are captured as `{job_id, ok: False, error, status_code}` in a `results` array with outer 200; outer 200/`ok=False` when at least one row failed.

### Frontend — `frontend/src/components/dashboard/DashboardDrillDownModal.jsx`
- **Data-Integrity variant only** (income variants untouched, per spec).
- **Checkbox column** (shadcn `<Checkbox>`) prepended to the row table.
- **Header checkbox** with true `indeterminate` state via radix; select-all is **page-scoped** with a persistent hint "Selects visible rows only."
- **Sticky Bulk Resolve bar** appears when ≥1 row is selected: `N selected · [Assign to customer ▾] [Assign to tech ▾] [Soft-delete jobs] [Clear]`.
- **Class-aware button state** via `classSupports(refClass)`: irrelevant actions are disabled with a tooltip (e.g. "Not applicable for this issue class", "Only enabled when every selected row is a job-type orphan").
- **Inline confirm strip** with per-action summary (not generic): reassigns quote the resolved target name, destructive delete quotes irreversibility.
- **Destructive double-confirm** on soft-delete: first click flips the button label to `Confirm delete N job(s)` in red; second click fires.
- **Client-minted `bulk_batch_id`** via `crypto.randomUUID()` (with fallback) — included on every POST for idempotency.
- **Client batch-cap short-circuit** matches backend cap (100).
- **Partial failure UX** — succeeded rows fade + drop from the table; failed rows stay + surface a dedicated `bulk-resolve-failed-list` block with per-row reasons; toast summarises `Resolved N/M · X failed`.
- **PortalErrorBoundary** wrapping preserved (exactly one, still labelled `dashboard-drilldown`).

### Tests
- **Pytest** `backend/tests/test_k41b_bulk_resolve.py` — 11 tests, 10 pass + 1 environmental skip (customer login 429, matching K41 pattern):
  - happy path (soft-delete) + shared `bulk_batch_id` on every audit event
  - happy path (bulk assign to a real customer)
  - non-admin roles → 403 (parametrized × 3)
  - unauthenticated → 401/403
  - > 100 items → 400 `batch_cap_exceeded`; empty items → 400 `items_required`
  - partial failure → per-row status (good + missing job id)
  - partial failure → per-row status (good + missing customer target)
  - idempotency → same batch id within TTL returns identical response with `replayed: true`, and NO additional audit rows
- **Vitest** `frontend/src/test/k41b-bulk-resolve-modal.test.jsx` — 21/21 pass. Coverage: checkbox column wiring, header indeterminate state, visible-rows-only scope, sticky bar test-ids, class-support enablement matrix, confirm strip summary shape, destructive two-step, `crypto.randomUUID` + BULK_CAP, partial failure list wiring, single-boundary invariant, income-variant scope exclusion.
- **Regression** — K41 pytest 16 pass + 3 skips; K41 vitest 20/20 pass; K42 unaffected.

## Phase K41c · Feb-2026 — Undo Last Bulk (10-minute window, SHIPPED)

### Backend — `backend/routers/dashboard_drilldown.py`
- **New endpoint** `POST /api/dashboard/data-integrity/undo-bulk` (admin + super).
- Body: `{ bulk_batch_id: string }`.
- Behaviour:
  1. Fetch every `dashboard_drilldown_edit` audit row with matching `bulk_batch_id`.  Missing batch → **404** `batch_not_found`.
  2. Newest audit row older than 10 min → **410** `window_expired`.
  3. Any pre-existing `dashboard_drilldown_bulk_undone` for the batch → **409** `already_undone`.
  4. Otherwise reverse each row: `soft_delete` → restore prior status + clear `deleted_*`; `customer_id`/`technician_id` assign → restore the audit's `before` value (and best-effort denorm name from the current customer/user).
  5. Emit **companion audit** `dashboard_drilldown_bulk_undone` per row with `undone_from_batch_id` linking back to the source batch, plus a fresh `undo_batch_id`.
  6. Idempotency — separate 60s TTL cache (`_bulk_undo_idempotency_cache`); replay returns identical response with `replayed: true` and NO extra mutations / audit rows.
- Returns `{ ok, bulk_batch_id, undo_batch_id, total, restored: [{job_id, field, restored_to}], failed: [{job_id, error}] }`.  Hard-deleted jobs surface in `failed` with `job_not_found`.

### Frontend — `DashboardDrillDownModal.jsx`
- **`UndoBanner`** component renders inside the sticky zone, directly below `BulkResolveBar`.
- Fires only after a successful bulk resolve — `handleBulkComplete` receives action metadata `(okIds, {bulkBatchId, action, mode, targetLabel})` and arms `lastBulk` with `expiresAt = now + 10 min`.
- Per-action summary shape:
  - Delete → red banner, "Soft-deleted N orphan jobs."
  - Customer assign → blue banner, "Reassigned N orphan jobs to <target>."
  - Tech assign → blue banner, "Reassigned N jobs to <target>."
- Countdown (`expires in mm:ss`) ticks via `setInterval(setNow(Date.now()), 1000)`.  At 0:00 the button set collapses to a single Dismiss button.
- `[Undo]` click flips to an inline `Cancel / Confirm — undo N changes` strip.  Confirm fires the endpoint.
- On success — toast `Restored N rows`, banner cleared, drilldown re-fetched by bumping `reloadKey` (fetch effect now keyed on `[url, reloadKey]`).
- On partial failure — `undo-banner-failed-list` block enumerates each failed row with its per-row reason.
- Closing the modal drops `lastBulk` from the DOM — no global undo tray (per spec).

### Tests
- **Pytest** `backend/tests/test_k41c_undo_bulk.py` — 9 tests, 8 pass + 1 environmental skip (customer login rate-limit): happy soft-delete + audit-chain integrity; happy assign-customer reverting `before` value; 11-min-old batch → 410; already-undone → 409 (bypass idempotency by pre-seeding the companion audit row); missing batch → 404; hard-deleted job → per-row `failed: job_not_found`; non-admin (parametrized ×3) → 403; idempotent replay stamps `replayed: true` with zero extra companion audits.
- **Vitest** `frontend/src/test/k41c-undo-bulk.test.jsx` — 17 tests, 17 pass.  Source-body assertions for banner test-ids, countdown wiring, summary shape, undo endpoint POST body, two-step confirm, refetch key wiring, K41b bar hand-off metadata; regression guards ensuring the bar no longer self-sticks (wrapper owns it) and both bar + banner live in the same sticky zone.
- **Combined regression** — K41 pytest 16 pass + 3 skips · K41 vitest 20/20 · K41b pytest 10 pass + 1 skip · K41b vitest 21/21 · K41c pytest 8 pass + 1 skip · K41c vitest 17/17.  **Zero regression.**

### Screenshots (persisted under `/app/artifacts/k41c/`)
- `k41c_sticky_after_scroll.png` — bar remains anchored after scrolling the row list.
- `k41c_undo_banner.png` — red destructive banner with `expires in 09:58` countdown, `Resolved 2/2 rows` toast, and the two soft-deleted rows dropped from the visible list.
- `k41c_restored.png` — post-undo state: `Restored 2 rows` toast, banner dismissed, table re-fetched with the restored rows back.

### Audit event discriminator decision
Chose a **companion event type** `dashboard_drilldown_bulk_undone` (rather than a discriminator on `dashboard_drilldown_edit`) — three reasons:
- Cleaner queries for both the K41b bulk-undo already-undone gate and any future forensic report ("which batches were rolled back?") — a single `event_type` predicate.
- The reversed mutation is semantically a distinct action, not a re-emission of the original edit.
- Keeps the K41b payload shape stable — no risk of downstream consumers reading `dashboard_drilldown_edit` rows and mis-classifying reverts.

Both events are joined by `undone_from_batch_id` → `bulk_batch_id` for the full audit trail.

### Follow-ups (deferred)
- None inside K41c scope.

## Phase K72 · Feb-2026 · EMERGENCY — "no-filter" Customer Email Diagnosis + Kill Switch — DIAGNOSED · KILL SWITCH SHIPPED (default OFF)

**Incident summary**
116 real customers on tenant `affdfbfa-88b9-4baa-ae45-2ef78531b6e4` (Pool & Landscaping of Vistancia) received email with subject/body "no-filter" from `cs@plofv.com` on 2026-08-31 20:59:33–57 UTC. Three replied confused: Michelle Moore, Scott Muir, Alan Chesebrough.

**Root cause**
`/app/backend/tests/test_bug_g_mass_messaging_filters.py::test_send_no_filters_still_works` authenticates against `admin@aquaterra.com` — which is the **production** tenant (no separate test tenant exists) — and POSTs `/api/mass-messaging/send` with `audience="all_active_customers", subject="no-filter", body="no-filter"`. The `APP_ENV=production` gate on the preview pod short-circuits the `guard_outbound` env check to `production_live`, so all 118 payloads flowed through Resend to real inboxes.

**Kill switch (SHIPPED, default OFF)**
- `FEATURE_CUSTOMER_EMAIL_KILL_SWITCH=on` in backend/.env → all `audience="customer"` sends short-circuit to a `dry_run` envelope regardless of `APP_ENV` (including production).
- `audience="internal"` explicitly tagged on 6 admin/staff paths (K63 lead alerts, K30 password reset, daily/weekly digests, leads_side_effects internal notifications) so they keep flowing during a customer-comms incident.
- Kill switch fires BEFORE the `APP_ENV=production` short-circuit AND before the K30 `allow_off_allowlist=True` bypass.
- 20 pytest cases green.

**Not yet fixed — user adjudicates**
Fix options A/B/C in `/app/memory/PHASE_K72_EMERGENCY_NO_FILTER_EMAIL_DIAG.md`. Recommended: Option C (test-tenant guard on `/api/mass-messaging/send` + rewire the offending test to a synthetic tenant + CI-only mass-messaging block).

**Blocked**
K70 tile theming paused mid-flight (no code committed to K70). R1 Financial suite on hold. All other queued items on hold until K72 fix ships.
